# MindRoom Chat Changes

## Runbook

### Equal-peer project discussion (2026-10-27)

- Parallel projects opt into the parent backend's peer discussion policy: members decide independently whether to speak and send separate Matrix messages under their own identities.
- Peers read the latest thread before deciding, may respond directly to each other, and do not automatically form a team report; explicitly invoking a named team remains available.
- A newer human message supersedes waiting responses to older messages, and bounded autonomous exchanges allow the conversation to pause without requiring every member to speak.
- Real Matrix checks verified untagged participation, peer-to-peer follow-up, a pause request, and resumption after new information; the original blood-pressure project was enabled without replacing its room or members.
- Root Python hooks and the vendored client's npm lint, typecheck, build, and tests are checked separately; the two known client failures concern scheduled-time formatting and caption upload recovery.

### Start another project from the wizard (2026-10-27)

- The header offers New Project and Chat; New Project creates an independent saved draft and preserves existing projects, Bots, and rooms.
- Each displayed draft is pinned in the page URL so refresh restores that project even after another tab creates a new one.
- Failed creation preserves the previous project and composer; concurrent clicks create only one draft.
- Independent review found no blocking issues; wizard tests (10), focused Python API/provisioning tests (15), typecheck, targeted lint, and production build pass.
- Live Chrome verification on port 3004 opened a fresh editable draft, retained it after refresh, and independently confirmed the previous project's saved room remained unchanged.
- Full frontend test run: 6934 passed; the same two previously recorded failures remain in scheduled-time formatting and caption upload recovery, outside the wizard changes.

### Local real Matrix project flow verified (2026-10-27)

- Synapse now runs locally through Colima, and the full MindRoom process provisions the saved project instead of the dashboard-only API.
- Start chat authenticates/selects the configured project owner on the correct homeserver before opening the native room route; failures stay visible and retryable.
- Real provisioning verifies the frozen owner's invitation as well as Bot membership and forbids reopening a plan after its config is committed.
- Project bots use thread mode so replies follow the current native Chat discussion.
- Actual room creation, three Bot joins plus Team, browser login handoff, browser Team message/reply, same-thread reply, restart recovery and unchanged repeat confirmation were verified.
- Local setup, startup script and evidence live under ignored .baspowers/sdd/wizard-real; credentials are never committed.
- Focused API/import checks (44), frontend wizard tests (6), type checks and build pass; unrelated provider_setup Tach failure remains.

### Agent Room durable drafts, confirmation, and real provisioning — Task C–E (2026-10-27)

- Task C adds owner-scoped saved drafts, conversation history, server revisions, name edits, and explicit two-step confirmation. Task D/E now map a confirmed proposal to real managed Agent/Team configuration and a real managed Matrix room; the result opens the native Chat room route.
- `/api/project-wizard/drafts` creates an empty draft; `/drafts/latest` and `/drafts/{id}` restore it; `/messages`, `PATCH /drafts/{id}`, `/confirm`, and `/reopen` implement versioned actions.
- The original stateless `/chat` route now returns 410 with instructions to preserve old page content and reload, so cached clients cannot receive false persistence promises.
- The first confirmation click opens a summary; the second freezes the revision and idempotency key, writes deterministic project config, waits for runtime reload and verifies every managed account joined the room before reporting success. A dashboard-only process returns an actionable 503 instead of a false success.
- Pending messages survive refresh, retry with their original message identity, and retain the prior proposal on model failure.
- Interrupted confirmations recover as retryable failures; completed confirmations survive restart and replay as the same explicitly simulated result.
- The project entry asks the network for the current shell before using offline fallback, avoiding an obsolete wizard served by the Chat service worker.
- Validation: 46 focused API/import tests, 33 wizard/navigation/service-worker tests, focused type checks and lint, and production build pass.
- Real-model generation, browser two-step confirmation, refresh recovery, duplicate confirmation, and API restart recovery passed.
- Full pytest still reports 72 failures outside wizard tests; full Chat Vitest reports 716 passing files and two failing files (scheduled-time formatting and caption restoration), both seen before Task C.

### Enable the computer screen's input only after Take control (2026-10-22)

- Problem: the Computer panel took the session's `mode` from the server unchecked, so a server that answered `control` for a new session got the screen's input enabled and keyboard focus moved into it, without the user pressing Take control.
  A computer server published by another agent in the room could do this when that agent's `show_computer` notice opened the panel, and the user's next keystrokes went to that server.
- Fix: `ComputerSessionClient` reports `control` only after its own `take` succeeded; every other status it returns, including the new session's, reads `view`.
  MindRoom's server starts every session in watch mode, so nothing changes with it.
- Tests: `api.test.ts` "reports control only after this client took it": a server that always answers `control` reads `view` until `take` and again after `release` (fails without the change).

### Mark a room unread only for a message, also when the read position is not loaded (2026-10-22)

- Problem: when the user's read position was not in the loaded live timeline, `roomHaveUnread` marked the room unread if any main-timeline event was loaded, not only a message.
  An agent's own state events (`io.mindroom.background_jobs`), reactions and redactions never show, but they counted, so the room kept an unread dot that opening it did not clear; only Mark as read did.
  In an agent room the conversation happens in threads, so the main-timeline receipt can stay on an old event for weeks, outside the loaded slice.
- Fix: `roomHaveUnread` returns true only for a notification event (`isNotificationEvent`) newer than the read position, whether or not that position is loaded.
  This is the rule it already followed when the position is loaded.
  Trade-off: a message in the unloaded gap behind later state or reactions no longer shows a dot of its own; the server's notification count still marks it, except in rooms set to mentions only.
- Tests: `room.test.ts` "ignores an agent's background state, reactions and redactions when the read position is not loaded" (fails without the change); the existing case for another member's message with an unloaded read position still counts it as unread.

### Find the MindRoom server from the agents in the user's rooms (2026-10-22)

- Why: hosted Chat ships `mindroom.computers.apiUrl` empty, so every user had to type their MindRoom address under Computers before Connections or Computers worked, and Chat showed a Computer button for every agent once a URL was set, even agents without a worker computer.
- Backend dependency: mindroom-ai/mindroom#3058 (`io.mindroom.server`): every MindRoom agent, team, and the router publishes room state keyed by its own user ID, `{"api_origin": <origin>, "computer": <bool>}`, on every join.
  The origin is the backend's OpenID audience (`MINDROOM_PUBLIC_URL`, or `http://localhost:<MINDROOM_PORT>`), so a token Chat binds to it verifies there.
  Matrix accepts a state key that starts with `@` only from that user, so only the agent itself can write it; managed rooms give the type power level 0.
- Design:
  - `matrix/agentRoomState.ts` owns who may describe themselves in room state, for this and `io.mindroom.background_jobs`: the state key is the sender, the sender is a MindRoom agent on the viewer's homeserver, and an agent known to have left is ignored (one whose membership is not loaded yet counts as joined).
    `useAgentRoomStateVersion` refreshes on that type, agent membership, and live-state resets.
    The jobs contract now only parses and orders.
  - `server/mindroomServer.ts` parses `api_origin` (through `resolveComputerApiUrl`) and `computer`; `server/useMindroomServers.ts` lists a room's servers and every origin in the user's joined rooms.
  - A published origin is used only while the homeserver binds tokens.
    Whether to offer one is asked of the homeserver once per client (`readOpenIdBinding` from `useBindsOpenIdTokens`, a fresh `/versions` request), never read from the cached versions, which outlive a rollback.
    A check that could not reach the homeserver is asked again on the next mount, and the check bypasses the HTTP cache.
    A token for a published origin is requested only after a new check (`requestAudienceOpenIdToken(..., { requireBinding: true })`), by the Connections card and the Computer panel, so a homeserver that stopped binding gets no token sent there.
    The check runs again after the token is issued, and the token is dropped unless binding still holds, so binding switched off during the request cannot hand that origin an unbound token.
    A homeserver that cannot be asked fails that request with a `ConnectionError`, so the Computer panel retries it as it does an unreachable homeserver.
  - Order: the user's Computers setting, then the deployment's `apiUrl`, then a published origin; a user who turned computers off keeps them off, and an unusable deployment value counts as unset.
  - In a room, each agent opens its own published server (`ComputerAgent.serverUrl`), so a room with agents of two MindRooms opens each one's computer on its own backend; with a configured URL, agents carry none.
    The Computer action shows only for agents that publish `computer: true`.
    With a configured URL, an agent whose MindRoom does not publish its server yet keeps the action, as before; while discovering, such an agent has no server to open and gets none.
  - Settings, General: every origin found gets its own **Open Connections** button with its address beside it, so a hostile agent cannot pass its portal off as the user's own; the Computers field shows the found origin as its placeholder while the setting follows the default.
  - In the native apps a published `localhost` server is the phone itself, so it is ignored.
  - The canvas index recorder runs when any of these origins exists, as it did for a configured one.
- No new catalog keys: the address beside a button and the placeholder are data, not text.
- Tests: `agentRoomState.test.ts` (self-description, homeserver, left agents), `mindroomServer.test.ts` (origin, computer flag, order, loopback origins), `useMindroomServers.test.tsx` (an agent that moves server and leaves, unrelated state, a retried check, a localhost server in the native apps), `openidAudience.test.ts` (a fresh, uncached check before a published server's token and again after it is issued; none when the homeserver does not bind, says off, stops binding, is unreachable, or errors, the last two as a `ConnectionError`), `ComputerPanel.test.tsx` (a found agent opens its own server after the checks; no token once binding is off), `MindroomConnectionsSettings.test.tsx` (found servers named and labelled, several by address, the configured server winning, a server turned off staying off, the fresh check only for found servers), `MindroomComputerSettings.test.tsx` (the placeholder), `Room.test.ts` (the Computer action with a found server, without binding, without a computer, without publishing, with an unusable deployment URL, a configured URL winning, each found agent's own server, and no computer for a silent agent while discovering), and `MindroomClientNonUIFeatures.test.ts` (the recorder for a found server only while the homeserver binds).
  Mutation checks failed the matching tests for each of: any state key, any homeserver, left agents kept, a truthy computer flag, oldest first, a loose binding answer, a failed check counted as binding, no fresh check before a token or after it is issued, the card or panel skipping it, the HTTP cache allowed, a failed check kept forever, an unreachable check made final or treated as binding, the panel ignoring the agent's server, the room giving agents no server, binding ignored in the room or globally, the found origin ignored, a turned-off service ignored, an unusable deployment URL blocking discovery, a found server left unnamed or unlabelled, no placeholder, agents without published state hidden with a configured URL or kept while discovering, and a localhost server kept in the native apps.
- Not caused by this change: `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` ("restores an already-cleared caption…") and `native/xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` also fail on `dev` here.

### Add a thread's fetched and buffered history to the SDK as history, not live events (2026-10-21)

- Report: opening the iPhone app froze it in a thread for many seconds; the owner thinks this started in the last weeks.
- Export (build `119ce345`): the WebContent process had been killed in the background, so the app cold-started into a thread after 11.7 h.
  The heartbeat stopped 4 s after start and resumed 26.4 s later (`heartbeat_gap`).
  Right after the gap, 1,379 cache transactions were open (1,071 read-write); each waited about 15.5 s, and 1,132 newer ones were still open at export.
  Of those that settled in the export's last 2.5 s, 542 were thread saves of the shape a single live event makes (`events`, `meta`, `attachments`, `attachment_references`, `room_ledger`), 273 the redaction check before a thread save, and none room saves.
  The trace's memory buffer kept only those 2.5 s (2,190 earlier events dropped) and the stored trace timed out on read, so the freeze itself is not in the export.
- Reproduction (production build, unminified, Chromium with iPhone 13 emulation and 4x CPU throttling, local Tuwunel): an agent thread of 300 replies, each with a 🛑 reaction and 3 streamed edits, plus 100 more sent after the thread was last open; then a cold start at the thread's URL.
  With the thread cached, the longest task was 1.1 s. With the thread never opened, it was 5.5 s, followed by 76 per-event thread saves (412 transactions in all), the export's pattern.
  93% of that task was `runThreadReconcilePass` > `addFetchedEventsToThread` > `Thread.addEvents(…, false)`: the open's reconcile appended the fetched reactions and edits newer than the SDK's first page, and the SDK announced each as a live event.
  For each, `roomLiveRenderController` called `setSupplementalThreadEvents(threadId, [event])`, which merges and re-hydrates the whole supplemental set (redaction lookups through the SDK's linear `findEventById`), so the cost grows with the fetched events times the thread's length.
  The sync engine then saved each live event in its own transaction, and each edit's target again when its compaction fired.
- Cause: the SDK's `Thread.addEventToTimeline` announces everything it appends as live (`fromCache: false`).
  #370 moved a reconcile's history older than the SDK window to backfill, but events newer than the window's first event stayed appended, and a reply's reactions and edits are newer than the reply.
  The same holds for the relations an unopened thread buffers since #360 (every reaction, and the newest edit of each reply, from the saved sync and live sync): `Thread.initialize()` replays them through `addEvent`, and a real-SDK test with 600 buffered relations gave 600 live events and 600 engine writes, plus one `ThreadEvent.Update` and a synthesized read receipt per event from the thread's own listener.
  None of these events needs the live path: the reconcile already persists its batch (`persistRepair`) and hands it to the render (`onRepaired`), and the open's SDK bootstrap saves the whole SDK thread timeline after `initialize()` (`threadOpenSdkBootstrap.ts`).
- Fix (SDK patch):
  - `Thread.addEventsAsHistory(events)` appends like `addEvents(events, false)`, but the timeline events carry `liveEvent: false`.
    Replies still count and announce `ThreadEvent.NewReply`, so thread lists and counts behave as before.
    `addFetchedEventsToThread` uses it for both of its appends; backfill is unchanged.
  - Both replay sites in `updateThreadMetadata` go through `replayBufferedEvents`, which adds the buffer the same way and skips the thread's own timeline listener (synthesized receipts, metadata refresh); the `ThreadEvent.Update` at the end of initialization covers it, and after the first page also the replay's `TimelineReset`.
    The buffer holds only reactions and edits, so reply counts are unaffected.
    On a server without thread support, `addEvent` itself still announces and refreshes per replayed event, as before.
  - Aggregation is unchanged: reactions count and edits apply as before.
- Behavior change: live-event listeners no longer see these events.
  The open thread gets them through `onRepaired` (one `setSupplementalThreadEvents` for the batch) and the SDK timeline refresh, without per-event auto-scroll or live-tail tracking.
  When a reconcile appends a newest event before sync delivers it, sync's copy is a duplicate the SDK drops, so that event is never live: no auto-scroll, expand-once, notification or sound for it, no immediate unread recompute (the server's counts still update it), and an agent UI action in it is not run (`chatUiController` acts on live events only).
  In encrypted rooms the engine no longer schedules a decrypted save for these events; the reconcile's backfill already behaved so.
  A card that only shows a thread no longer caches its buffered relations; the next open fetches and saves them.
- Tests:
  - `reconciler.sdkThread.test.ts`: the reconcile's append of events newer than the SDK window, and its append to a window that starts at the root, announce no live event (4 each before), with the same two new replies announced.
  - `matrixSdkThreadBootstrapRequests.test.ts`: opening a deferred thread whose saved sync held 30 replies with 30 reactions and 30 edits announces no live event and at most two `ThreadEvent.Update`s, applies the latest reply's edit and counts an older reply's reaction.
    It fails without the change (60 live events), and with only the listener skip removed (62 updates).
- Validation:
  - The same reproduction with the fix: the reconcile's 5.5 s task is gone (longest task 1.1 s, during startup, as before), the longest main-thread gap drops from 5.6 s to 1.5 s, long tasks in the first 20 s from 14.3 s to 9.4 s, and IndexedDB transactions from 412 to 83, with 4 thread saves instead of 76.
    The thread shows the same rows on both builds: the final edit of every reply and its 🛑 chip, at the bottom and after scrolling up.
  - The patch applies to a fresh `matrix-js-sdk@41.7.0` and reproduces the patched files.
  - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings) pass; Prettier passes on the changed files.
  - `npx vitest run`: 6,870 passed and the 4 known failures on `dev` (`xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` 3, `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` 1).
  - Not checked on an iPhone; WebKit's IndexedDB timings differ from Chromium's.
- PR #492 review (Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, both approved at `753302bf`): added the root-first append test both asked for (it fails with that append reverted) and the notification, sound and unread effects Opus listed.
  Declined: restoring the previous `addingHistory` value on exit (no call nests) and keeping a fetched page's strictly newer tail live (Opus, optional; the race is documented above and the SDK's first page has the same one).
- Next:
  - The saved sync's replay at startup still announces thread events as live, because `Room.addLiveEvents` does not pass `fromCache` on to threads; the reproduction counted 500 before `PREPARED`, cheap because the engine ignores them and the UI was not mounted yet.
  - `setSupplementalThreadEvents` re-hydrates its whole set per call and `EventTimelineSet.findEventById` scans linearly; a burst of genuinely live thread events still pays both.
  - Storage events filled the deep trace's memory buffer within 2.5 s and the stored trace timed out, which hid the freeze; the next export should keep the seconds before a long task.

### Soft, outlined buttons everywhere (2026-10-20)

- Why: solid folds buttons read as bright pills in dark themes: a white "View computer" under an agent's UI request, a lavender and salmon pair in the computer panel, and the same in settings (Save computer service, Use app default, Open Connections), dialogs, auth and room settings.
  A `Button` without `fill` is solid, so most of them never asked for it.
- Change: every text `Button` that was solid (no `fill`, `fill="Solid"`, or a conditional `Solid`) is now `fill="Soft"` and `outlined`, with `radii="300"` where it had no radius (`size="500"` buttons keep the default, like the sign-in buttons beside them): 147 buttons, the computer panel's 6 included.
  Soft buttons get the same treatment, so a converted button matches its neighbours: 62 gain an outline and 36 without a radius get `radii="300"`.
  That is 215 buttons in 102 files in all, plus 49 spinners inside converted buttons that move to `fill="Soft"`.
  Other variants are unchanged, so unsaved and destructive states still differ by color; buttons with `fill="None"` keep it.
  Where only the solid fill had told actions apart, the variant now does: Retry is `Primary` and Clear cache `Secondary` beside the `Critical` Remove account (`ClientRoot.tsx`) and Continue (`SpecVersions.tsx`), and an incoming call's Reject is `Critical` (Ignore `Secondary` in rooms) beside the green Answer.
  Unselected toggles (room timeline view, Connect's account choice) are `fill="None"` without an outline, since a soft `Secondary` fill is darker than the selected soft `Primary` in light themes and a `fill="None"` outline draws in the variant's main color.
  "Sign in with Apple" (`SSOLogin.tsx`) stays solid, because Apple prescribes its appearance.
  `ChatUiActionButton` also switches to `Primary` with button text `B300` and an icon per action (Monitor, Setting, Category, User); `ComputerPanel` shares its props in `actionButtonProps`, and the MindRoom settings buttons move from body text to `B300`.
  `docs/ui-design.md` records the rule.
  Behavior and labels are unchanged.
- Tests: the `ChatUiActionProvider.test.tsx` folds mock gains `Icon` and `Icons`; the `ComputerPanel.test.tsx` and `CanvasPanel.test.tsx` mocks keep `outlined` off the DOM.
- Validation: typecheck, ESLint and Prettier on the changed files, and build pass; the unit suite passes except the 4 known failures on `dev` (`xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` 3, `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` 1).
  `e2e/agent-ui-actions.spec.ts` passes against a local Tuwunel.
  Temporary Playwright specs (local Tuwunel; for the panel, a mocked computer API and a minimal RFB server so it connects) captured the request button, the panel's watch and control actions, login, create room, the Computers, Connections and Device Verification settings cards, in light and dark, before and after.
- Not covered: the 35 solid `Badge`s (4 of them conditional), including the emoji board's Sticker and Emoji tabs (`as="button"`), and `IconButton`s.
  A solid button that stood out from neutral neighbours of the same variant now looks like them: Create room among Home's actions, Next beside Previous in Explore.
- PR #484 review at `865fcaec`: Sol and Astra approved; Opus found Retry looking like Remove account, Reject like Answer, toggles reading backwards in light themes, and size-500 sign-in buttons getting a different radius from the SSO buttons beside them, all fixed above.
  Also done: a redundant `variant="Primary"` dropped and the `ComputerPanel` mock no longer passes `data-outlined`.
  Kept: `ChatUiActionButton`'s icons (shown to and approved by the owner) and `actionButtonProps`, which six buttons share.
- PR #484 review at `b76ce53f`: Sol and Astra approved; Opus found the config-load dialog's Sign in again / Retry still looking like Continue offline (`ConfigConfig.tsx`, now `Primary`), and that unselected toggles' outline drew a near-white ring in dark themes (now no outline).
- PR #484 review at `6df008a1`: Opus, Sol and Astra approved; Opus's nits are done: the pending Review button drops `outlined`, since `ReviewButtonPending` draws its own warning ring, and the radius rule names buttons with their own radius.

### Keep the server's pinned power levels in new voice rooms (2026-10-20)

- Problem: voice rooms from the create-room dialog and agent call rooms were created with a `power_level_content_override` whose `events` held only the call-membership level.
  Tuwunel and Synapse replace the whole default `events` map with the override's, so the levels they pin in every new room were lost: `m.room.power_levels`, `m.room.history_visibility`, `m.room.encryption` and `m.room.server_acl` at 100, and `m.room.tombstone` at 100 (150 in room versions with privileged creators).
  Those events fell back to `state_default` (50), so moderators could change power levels, history visibility, encryption and the server ACL, and upgrade the room.
- Fix: `createVoiceRoomPowerLevelsOverride` (`src/app/components/create-room/utils.ts`) restates those levels next to `org.matrix.msc3401.call.member` at 0, and takes the room version for the tombstone level.
  Agent call rooms leave the version to the server, so their tombstone stays at 100, which lets the creator upgrade the room in any version.
  Existing rooms keep their power levels.
- Tests: `src/app/components/create-room/utils.test.ts` checks the override `createRoom` sends for a version 11 and a version 12 voice room, and the agent call room test in `agentCall.test.ts` checks its full override; all three fail without the fix.

### Keep menus, dialogs and shortcuts on the app's portal container (2026-10-20)

- Problem: `App.tsx` and `hasBlockingPortalOverlay` looked `#portalContainer` up by id on every render and every check.
  Message-extras HTML keeps SVG `id` attributes, and a message comes before the real container in the page, so a message with an `<svg id="portalContainer">` took its place while on screen: keyboard shortcuts and edge-swipes treated the SVG's children as an open overlay and stopped, and after a layout breakpoint change menus and dialogs rendered into the SVG, where they were invisible.
- Fix: `portalOverlay.ts` looks the container up once, at startup, and exports it; `App.tsx` and `hasBlockingPortalOverlay` use that element.
- Tests: `portalOverlay.test.ts` adds an `<svg id="portalContainer">` to the page after startup; shortcuts are not blocked and the exported container is still the app's (fails without the change: the SVG counts as an open overlay).

### Show every call's fields in a folded approval group (2026-10-20)

- Problem: a group of several calls of one tool, folded behind "Show N calls" with "Approve all N once", previewed fields merged from the first call's keys only (`mergeArgumentFields`).
  A field only a later call carried, such as `cc` on a second `send_email`, was missing from the preview.
- Fix: the merged preview takes the keys of every call, in first-seen order, and the usual target-first ordering still applies.
  A field some calls lack is merged like a value that differs between calls: the values present are joined.
- Tests: `argumentFields.test.ts` merges `{ to }` with `{ to, cc }` and expects `cc` (fails without the change).

### Merge an edit into a search result only from the message's sender (2026-10-20)

- Problem: message search merged an edit (`m.replace`) into the result of the message it names without checking who sent the edit, and kept the newer of the two.
  So an edit another member sent, naming someone else's message, showed in place of that message's result and hid it; the timeline ignores such edits.
- Fix: `getCanonicalSearchEventKey` includes the sender, so `deduplicateResults` and the merge across pages in `MessageSearch` fold an edit only into a message from the same sender.
  Someone else's edit stays a result of its own, as an edit does when the message it names does not match the search.
- Tests: `useMessageSearch.test.ts` "merges an edit into the original only when the same sender sent both": another member's edit leaves the original result in place (fails without the change), and the sender's own edit still replaces it.

### Follow the encrypted-room URL preview setting in pinned messages and the inbox (2026-10-20)

- Problem: the Pinned Messages panel (`RoomPinMenu`) and the Notifications inbox showed URL previews whenever `urlPreview` was on, so turning off URL previews in encrypted rooms (`encUrlPreview`) still showed, and fetched, previews for links in encrypted rooms there.
  The timeline already used `encUrlPreview` for encrypted rooms; both views come from Cinny, which has the same gap.
- Fix: both views pass `encUrlPreview` for rooms with `room.hasEncryptionStateEvent()` and `urlPreview` otherwise, as `useTimelineMessageFeature` does.
- Tests: `RoomPinMenu.test.ts` "uses the encrypted-room URL preview setting when encrypted is ..." renders a pinned message with `urlPreview` on and `encUrlPreview` off and checks the `urlPreview` prop the pin menu passes to `RenderMessageContent`: `false` in an encrypted room (fails without the change), `true` in an unencrypted one.
  `RenderMessageContent.test.ts` "passes a URL preview renderer on only with urlPreview on" checks that `RenderMessageContent` hands its content renderer no URL preview renderer when `urlPreview` is `false`.
- Not covered: the inbox has no component test.

### Match the typed name in the mention picker before its search answers (2026-10-19)

- Problem: typing `@Min` and pressing Tab quickly, or while the room's members loaded, could tag someone else.
  `UserMentionAutocomplete` listed, and Tab took the first of, the whole member list whenever `useAsyncSearch` had no result: until the search, which runs in an effect after paint, answered the typed text, and again each time `useRoomMembers` handed over a new array (after `loadMembersIfNeeded` and on every membership or power-level event), because the hook clears its result whenever its list changes.
  The demo director worked around it by waiting for the named member and clicking that option (demo#10).
- Fix: until the hook's result answers the typed text, `UserMentionAutocomplete` matches the members at once with `searchNow`, which finds what the hook would: the first 1,000 matches in list order, ordered by `orderSearchItems`.
  Because it runs during render, `searchNow` reads at most `SEARCH_NOW_SCAN_LIMIT` (5,000) members, about 2.5 ms, and says whether it read them all.
  If it found nobody and stopped short, Tab inserts nothing (neither a member nor a pill for the partial name) until the search answers; matches it did find are real matches, like the search's own first partial answer.
  `useAsyncSearch` itself is unchanged.
- Tests: `UserMentionAutocomplete.test.tsx` presses Tab before the search answers, after the member list changes, and after the list grows to include the named member; each takes the member matching `Min` (all fail without the change: Tab takes the first member).
  With the only match past the first 5,000 members, Tab inserts nothing before the search answers and that member after it (fails without the scan limit).
- Not covered:
  - `RoomMentionAutocomplete`, `EmoticonAutocomplete` and `CommandAutocomplete` also hand their first item to Tab, and still list everything until their search answers and again after their list changes.
    `MindroomCommandAutocomplete` does the same until its first answer (its list is constant).
  - A query with many matches still orders up to 1,000 of them during render (about 15 ms in a benchmark, whatever the room's size).

### One stale stop-chip filter in Reactions (2026-10-19)

- Problem: `Reactions` filtered stale stop chips twice: in the `useRelations` selector, which depended on `targetEvent` and so never re-ran when the final stream edit updated that event in place, and again per render to cover that miss (#466).
- Fix: the selector returns `getActiveAnnotationsByKey` unfiltered and the per-render `isStaleStopReactionKey` check is the only filter; it reads the target's current content on every render.
  No visible change.
- Tests: `Reactions.test.ts` "hides a stale stop chip once the target message proves a terminal stream" and "drops the stop chip once the target finishes streaming in place" pass, and both fail without the per-render check.

### Read thread replies only with thread and unthreaded receipts (2026-10-19)

- Problem: Chat counted a `main` receipt as reading older thread replies (`getEffectiveThreadReadUpToTs` took the later of the thread receipt and the room receipt).
  MSC3771 and the server do not: only thread and unthreaded receipts read thread events.
  So a main receipt cleared threads' unread cards and indicators while the server kept counting the replies, and the room badge stayed up with no unread thread to explain it.
- Fix: thread unread state (`getThreadUnread`) follows MSC3771 and honours only thread and unthreaded receipts, matching the server's counts.
  The room-receipt fallback and the `readUpToTs` plumbing that fed it are removed, and the cross-room thread index refreshes a room's threads on your unthreaded receipts only, not on main-timeline ones.
- Visible change: in the classic view, replies read only inline now stay unread until the thread is opened, matching the room badge, which already stayed up.
- Not covered: classic thread receipts for replies read inline, and the compact view's stuck room count (the morning-brief demo's "1"), are tracked separately.
- Tests:
  - `readReceipts.integration.test.ts`: a main receipt on a newer event leaves a thread's replies unread, an unthreaded receipt reads them (fails without the change).
  - `useCrossRoomThreadIndex.test.ts`: an unthreaded receipt refreshes the room's threads, a main-timeline one none.

### Edit messages too large for one event (2026-10-19)

- Problem: after long messages became long-text sidecars, a message you sent that way could not be edited, because `canEditEvent` offered editing only for text, emote and notice messages; Up arrow skipped it and edited an older message.
  An edit too large for one event failed like a long send: an edit carries its text twice (fallback and `m.new_content`), so it hit the 64 KiB limit at half the size, and Save just stopped spinning.
  Editing the latest content naively would also start from the event's 2,000-character preview, so saving would cut the message.
- Fix:
  - `canEditEvent` also offers editing your own `m.file` messages that carry a valid long-text sidecar (`getMindroomLongTextSource`).
  - `useMindroomEditableContent` loads the content the editor starts from: the latest edit or the message, with a long text downloaded whole through `hydrateCachedMindroomLongText` (usually already cached by the timeline). The editor is read-only and Save disabled until it has loaded, so nothing typed meanwhile is replaced; if it cannot load, the editor says "Failed to load message" and Save stays disabled, so a preview is never saved over the message.
  - `buildMindroomEditContent` sends an edit that fits one event as before.
    A larger one uploads the whole edit as a long-text sidecar, as MindRoom's backend does: MindRoom reads the file in place of the event and takes the message from its `m.new_content`, and Chat's reader does the same.
    The event then carries the sidecar's preview as `m.new_content`, with a `* ` fallback of the new content's type.
  - The new content takes its type from the loaded content, so shortening a long-text message turns it back into a text message.
  - `copyMindroomResolvedEditMetadata` no longer copies `io.mindroom.long_text` from older edits: the marker is true only beside its own file, and the copy into the latest edit, which can be the local echo of an edit about to be sent, put a stale marker on a short edit that followed a long one.
- Backend: no change; MindRoom finds the sidecar in an edit's `m.new_content` (`sidecar_content_to_resolve`) and reads the edited message from the file (`extract_edit_body`).
- Tests:
  - `longEdit.test.ts`: a small edit is unchanged; a large edit uploads the whole edit, which Chat reads back as the new content, its replacement is a long-text preview without a relation, and its fallback stays text; the editor content is the message as it is, the whole downloaded text, or nothing when only the preview comes back.
  - `room.test.ts`: your own long-text file is editable; an ordinary file and someone else's long text are not (fails without the change).
  - `editMetadata.test.ts`: a long-text marker is not copied into a later edit (fails without the change).
  - `e2e/live/long-composer-message.spec.ts` sends a 22 KB Markdown message, opens it with Up arrow, checks that the editor holds its last line, appends to it and saves, checks that the edit is a long-text sidecar whose file holds the whole edit, then edits it down to a short text and checks that the edit is plain text again; on the previous build Up arrow does not open the editor.
  The spec now shares one signed-in page across its cases, because the homeserver rate-limits a third login.
- Not covered:
  - An edit still fails without saying why when the upload or the send fails; the editor stays open, so nothing is lost.
  - No test types into the editor during a slow download; the timeline has usually cached the text already, and the editor is read-only until then.

### Send messages too large for one event as long-text sidecars (2026-10-19)

- Problem: a long Markdown message went back into the composer on every Send, with no error.
  Tuwunel refuses an event larger than 65,535 bytes (`M_TOO_LARGE`), and since the send recovery of 2026-10-02 a failed send returns its text to the composer and drops the unsent echo.
  The paste guard turns a paste into a pasted-text attachment once its estimate passes 56 KiB, but it estimates the formatted body as the escaped plain text, while the sent `formatted_body` is rendered Markdown, which for lists, tables and inline code is 1.5 to 3 times the text.
  With the composer's own serializer, Markdown of about 16 KB (a table) to 24 KB (mixed headings and lists) made events over the limit, while every such paste stayed inline; text typed after a paste is never checked.
- Fix: the send session measures the content it is about to send, relation included.
  Content over `MAX_EVENT_CONTENT_BYTES` (the 40,000-byte budget canvas answers use, which leaves room for encryption) is uploaded whole through `uploadMindroomLongTextSidecar`, and the event is an `m.file` preview with the first 2,000 characters (cut between characters), `[Message continues in attached file]`, and the message's mentions and relation.
  Chat shows such a message in full like any other, and MindRoom reads it as a text turn (`prepare_file_sidecar_text_event`), as it does for canvas answers.
  A failed upload throws before anything is sent, so the text returns to the composer as for any failed send.
  The paste guard is unchanged: one huge paste still becomes a pasted-text attachment.
- Reuse: the budget, `contentBytes` and the continuation note move from `canvasMessages.ts` to `messages/longText.ts`, beside the sidecar format, so canvas answers, canvas state and the composer share them; `buildMindroomLongTextPreview` builds the composer's preview.
- Tests:
  - `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts`: a 50 KB message is uploaded whole and sent as a preview with its thread relation and mentions, and a failed upload sends nothing and returns the text to the composer (both fail without the change); a short message is sent as it is.
  - `longText.test.ts`: the preview keeps the start of the text, the mentions and the relation, and does not split a surrogate pair (fails without the cut).
  - `e2e/live/long-composer-message.spec.ts` pastes 22 KB of Markdown into a room and into a thread on a local Tuwunel, sends it, and checks that the full text renders and that the server holds a long-text preview; on `dev` the message never reaches the timeline and the text is back in the composer.
- Not covered:
  - A message sent as a sidecar is an `m.file` event, which Chat does not offer to edit, and an edit too large for one event still fails; both are left for a follow-up.
  - A long `/me` or `/notice` message is sent as an `m.file` preview and shows as ordinary text.
  - A send that fails for another reason still returns its text without saying why.

### The stop button reads "Stop" (2026-10-18)

- Why: MindRoom's stop button is a 🛑 reaction the agent adds to its reply while it streams (backend `stop.py`, `docs/chat-commands.md` "Stop Button"); reacting 🛑 stops the reply.
  Chat drew it as an ordinary reaction, "🛑 1", whose tooltip said the agent "reacted with :octagonal_sign:", so in the demo recordings it read as a stray reaction or an error under every streaming reply.
- Change: `isAgentStopButton` (`stopReaction.ts`) picks out a 🛑 reaction sent by the reply's own sender while the reply's stream metadata says it is streaming.
  `Reactions` labels that chip "Stop" instead of its count and gives it the tooltip "Stop this reply"; `Reaction` takes an optional `label` shown in place of the count.
  Clicking still toggles the viewer's 🛑, which is what stops the reply, and stale stop chips stay hidden as before.
  `Reactions` also drops a stop chip on the render after the reply's final edit, which updates the target in place where the memoized stale filter doesn't see it.
  A person's 🛑, and one on a message without stream metadata, stay plain reactions.
  Strings are in all 17 catalogs.
- Tests: `Reactions.test.ts` checks the agent's chip is labelled Stop and a person's is counted, and that both toggle the viewer's 🛑; `stopReaction.test.ts` covers `isAgentStopButton` for another key, a person's reaction, a message without stream metadata, and a missing target.
- Validation: typecheck, ESLint and Prettier on the changed files, and the unit suite (the 3 known host-only `xcodeCloudPostClone` failures; load timeouts in RoomTimeline/RoomView files passed on a sequential rerun).
  A temporary Playwright spec against a local Tuwunel showed an agent's streaming thread reply with "🛑 Stop" and the tooltip "Stop this reply" in light and dark ("🛑 1" on `dev`); clicking it sent the viewer's 🛑 reaction, and a 👍 on a finished reply kept its count.

### Show which invite suggestion Enter picks, without the dialog showing through (2026-10-18)

- Problem: with the Invite dialog's suggestions open, the third row looked highlighted while the cursor and the keyboard choice were on the first (demo recording bring-the-team-in, 5-20 s).
  The lavender band was the dialog's own Invite button showing through the list, which uses the 60 % menu tint; the option Enter or Tab picks (`aria-selected`, moved with the arrow keys) had no fill at all, because the Folds menu row only fills on hover, keyboard focus and `aria-pressed`, and DOM focus stays in the input.
- Fix: `InviteAutocompleteOption` fills `aria-selected` rows with the Surface hover color, and the list uses the existing `glassDenseOverBackdrop` tint (94 %, 90 % in dark themes) because it covers the dialog's controls.
  While the input holds a valid MXID no option is marked (no fill, no `aria-activedescendant`), because Enter then invites the typed MXID, not a suggestion.
  The list still extends past the dialog (CINNY-217); that is intended, so long lists are not clipped.
- Tests: `dialog-menu-glass.spec.ts` checks that the invite list is tinted at least 90 % and that only the selected option is filled, in both themes and in Chromium and WebKit; each check fails without its half of the change.
  `InviteUserAutocomplete.test.tsx` checks that `aria-selected` follows the arrow keys and that a typed MXID marks no suggestion while Enter still submits it (the latter fails without the gate).

### Drop "Load Older Messages" from a thread whose cached copy reaches the root (2026-10-18)

- Why: the demo recordings showed "Load Older Messages" above brand-new two-message threads opened from the room overview (morning-brief, remind-me, whole-team-one-thread).
- Cause: when the thread's IndexedDB snapshot is complete and finishes loading before the SDK bootstrap, `useThreadSession` takes its complete-cache branch, which cleared the SDK's backward cursor only for a relations-proven snapshot.
  That cursor came from `Thread.initialize()`'s first recursive `/relations` page, and Tuwunel returns `next_batch` with every non-empty page, so it was always set and kept the chip.
  When the bootstrap finished first, `refreshLatestThreadSlice` fetched the next, empty page and cleared it, so the chip depended on which read won.
- Change (`useThreadSession.ts`): the complete-cache branch reconciles the cursor with the cached page through `reconcileCachedThreadBackwardToken`, as the partial-cache path does, with the page's start known.
  The cursor stays when the SDK holds replies older than the cached page; the open-time reconcile still repairs a snapshot whose reply count was wrong.
- Tests: `threadSession.test.tsx` covers a count-proven complete page clearing the cursor (fails without the change) and a page that starts after the SDK's replies keeping it.
- Validation: thread unit tests, typecheck, ESLint and Prettier on the changed files; a temporary Playwright spec against a local Tuwunel opened a streamed two-message thread from the overview with `/relations` delayed by 3 s so the cache won: the chip showed in 3 of 3 runs on `dev` and in 0 of 3 with the change.

### Fit the invited count in the Members header at the default width (2026-10-18)

- Problem: in a room with a pending invite, the Members drawer header read "4 Me… · 1 / Invited" at the drawer's default 266 px width (demo recording bring-the-team-in): the member count was truncated and the invited chip wrapped onto two lines.
  The header holds the count, the "·", the chip and two 40 px buttons; at 266 px the counts get 146 px but need about 181. The pending-invites change (2026-10-01) was not checked in a running client, and the live glass spec widens the drawer to 380 px.
- Fix: the invited chip moves under the member count, without the "·"; the chip keeps its button and click, loses its inline inset so its label lines up with the count, and truncates instead of wrapping. The header height is unchanged (54 px holds both lines).
  Both labels are capped at the column's width, since a column sizes them to their text and they would otherwise run under the buttons instead of truncating (at the 200 px minimum width the count now ends in an ellipsis; on `dev` it was squeezed to 0 px).
- Tests: `e2e/live/members-header-glass.spec.ts` resets the drawer to its default width and checks that neither "29 Members" nor "1 Invited" is truncated or reaches the buttons, then narrows it to 200 px and checks that the count stays clear of the buttons.
  It fails on `dev` ("29 Members is not truncated") and, without the width cap, at the narrow check; it passes in Chromium and WebKit, both themes.

### Give `[+all]` its own glass (2026-10-18)

- Why: in the demo recordings, the `[+all]` expand-all toggle at the top right of a thread was printed over the timestamp of whichever message had scrolled under it.
  The toggle sits in the clear band below the sticky thread banner (below the room header and overview in room view), where rows keep scrolling; #261 kept it there so it stays reachable.
  It was bare text without a surface, the only floating timeline control without one (Jump to Latest, Show more/less and the pagination chips use the control glass).

  The label's 70% opacity is gone, because it would also have thinned the glass.
- Residual: the chip keeps the toggle's old place, which is not aligned with the timestamp column (it ends 8 px short of it in a thread and covers all but its first 4 px in the room view), so a timestamp lined up with the chip can still show a sliver beside it, as content shows beside any floating chrome.

### List only users that contain the invite search, not near misses (2026-10-18)

- Problem: searching "tom" in the Invite dialog listed "8 matching users": Tom Becker, then Omar Haddad, Julia Santos and the agents Counsel, Euler, Forge, Ledger and Quill.
  None of the others contains "tom"; the homeserver's directory search returns only `@tom` for that term (checked against Tuwunel), so they came from Chat's own ranking.
- Root cause: `rankUsers` ranks the cached user directory with Fuse at threshold 0.4, which lets a three-letter query differ by one character ("om" in Omar, "tos" in Santos, "rom" in every `mindroom_` localpart).
  The CINNY-216 tiers already put these fuzzy-only matches last, but the list still filled its eight slots with them.
- Fix: once at least one user contains the query (tier below the fuzzy-only tier), fuzzy-only matches are left out; when nobody contains it, they are still listed, so a typo such as "alcie" still finds Alice.
- Tests: `userDirectorySearch.test.ts` checks that "tom" lists only Tom, that "alice" no longer lists "Elise Example", that a post-prefix hit drops a fuzzy display-name match, and that a typo still finds its user; the first three fail before the change.

### Reply quotes name mentioned members (2026-10-18)

- Report (demo review C2): a quoted reply read "↩ Forge @mindroom_quill:matrix.localhost Signups failed…" while the quoted message itself showed an `@Quill` pill.
- Root cause: MindRoom agents write mentions as full Matrix IDs in the plain body (`_entity_mention_resolution_from_user_id` in the backend's `matrix/mentions.py`); only the formatted body carries the pill.
  Reply quotes and the composer's reply bar preview the plain body through `getLocalizedThreadMessagePreviewText`, and only compact thread cards replaced Matrix IDs with display names afterwards.
- Change: `replaceMatrixUserIdsWithDisplayNames` moves from `compactThreadCardViewModel.ts` to `threadMessagePreview.ts` with an optional prefix, and the new `getReplyPreviewText` gives `Reply` and `RoomInputReplyPreview` the preview with room members shown as `@<display name>`, as the pill reads.
  Both compute it on every render rather than memoizing it, so names of lazily loaded members appear on the next render; the body analysis stays cached.
  Matrix IDs of non-members stay raw, as on thread cards, which keep their bare names.
- Unchanged by design: the `🔧 3 tools ·` badge and a table's cells set apart by middle dots in the same quote come from the shared preview formatter (#307 and "Compact view previews" below).
- Tests: `Reply.test.tsx` renders a quoted agent hand-off with two member mentions (one followed by a comma) and a non-member mention; it fails on `dev`.
- Next: none.

### App Store update 4.12.421 (2026-10-18, submitted)

- Status: App Review submission `df446230-d0f4-4e3d-8ad8-0d896c2c16ff` for `4.12.421 (415)` reached `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` at 17:04 UTC.

  WebKit keyboard checks press Option-Tab on macOS, and the Computers mock returns a nonretryable 400 instead of a now-retried 503.
  Prepend rides wheel into the auto-paginate trigger zone instead of teleporting to a fixed offset.
  The latency ride starts its slow route at a known frame and stays at least 720px inside the loaded window; a start that would slow its flick below 30px per step fails.
  The offline cache spec opens folded bodies by keyboard because the next message's hover toolbar can cover the button (#463).
- Validation: 6,825 unit tests, typecheck, lint (0 errors, 18 existing warnings), the iOS build, and the Ruby release suite (8 tests) pass.
  The full browser run passed 437 cases with 12 platform skips; the Computers worker test is blocked without the external `E2E_COMPUTER_FIXTURE`.
- Next: await App Review and address any Apple feedback; publication is automatic after approval.
  Fix #463 so the offline cache spec can click the folded-message button.

### Explain changing a canvas answer only when the page tries to (2026-10-18)

- Why: the demo recordings showed "To change your answer, discard this one first." under every staged canvas answer, so the confirm bar read like instructions for a case the user had not hit.
- Change (`CanvasPanel.tsx`): a staged answer stays frozen until Send or Discard, as before; the hint shows once the page submits a different answer (label or data) while one waits, which is when the bar would otherwise ignore the user's new choice; the same answer again, as from a double click, shows nothing. The **Data** disclosure stays: it is how the user sees exactly what will be sent, which the page's label need not match.

### Name a canvas by its title instead of the other-client fallback (2026-10-18)

- Why: the demo recordings showed every canvas in the timeline as "Interactive panel: Q4 launch review: pick a time. Open it in MindRoom Chat to respond." above **Open canvas**, and the answer's reply quote repeated it.
  That body is MindRoom's fallback for other Matrix clients; Chat rendered it for its own canvases too, telling the user to open the app they were in.
- Change: `readCanvasNoticeTitle` (`chatUiProtocol.ts`) reads the title of a `show_canvas` notice (version 1, a valid canvas).
  The timeline shows a canvas notice from a MindRoom agent as the panel icon and its title, with the existing button below (`data-canvas-notice-title`).
  Any sender can write the UI-action key, so a notice from anyone else keeps its body, as approval cards do.
  Previews (reply quotes, thread cards and lists, the minimap) name a canvas by its title, an update by its new one.
  So does the composer's reply bar: the reply draft carries the title as plain `previewText` (`roomInputDrafts.ts`, `roomTimelineReplyDraft.ts`), which `RoomInputReplyPreview` shows without a Markdown preview, naming members as the sent quote does, so titles such as `1. Pick a time` or `---` stay as written.

### Accept all Primary invites at once (2026-10-14)

- Why: the owner had 15 invites from their MindRoom router (one per agent room) and had to accept each by hand.
- Change: the Primary section of Inbox > Invites gets an "Accept All" chip in its header, in the same place and style as the Public section's existing "Decline All".
  The per-card join (join, then add a direct invite to `m.direct` under the guessed DM partner) moves to `inbox/acceptInvite.ts`; Accept All runs it for each invite through `rateLimitedActions`, so 429s back off and one failed join leaves that invite listed without stopping the rest.
  While the batch runs, the Primary cards' Accept and Decline are disabled (on that mount; switching filter tabs remounts the list while the batch keeps running), and the batch skips any room that is no longer an invite when its turn comes (resolved by a card or on another device).
  `addRoomIdToMDirect` and `removeRoomIdFromMDirect` (`utils/matrix.ts`) now run one at a time per client: each reads `m.direct` and writes it back whole, so two overlapping DM accepts (a card and the batch, or a second batch started after a tab switch) could each drop the other's room. matrix-js-sdk 41.7's `setAccountData` resolves after the sync echo, so each queued update reads the previous write. A write waiting on a stalled sync holds that client's later ones until sync resumes; the queue is per client because switching accounts stops the old client without a reload, and its pending write never settles.
  Accept All does not navigate; joined invites leave the list as they sync. Public and Spam get no Accept All: those invites come from strangers or flagged senders.
  New `sharedUi.invites.acceptAll` string in all 17 locales.
- Tests: `acceptInvite.test.ts` covers pending invites joined, a room no longer invited skipped, a failed join not stopping the batch, and `m.direct` written only for the DM that joined, with `is_direct` read before the join.
  `matrix.test.ts` covers two overlapping `addRoomIdToMDirect` calls keeping both rooms (fails without the queue), and one client's update completing while another client's write never settles (hangs with one shared queue).
  `e2e/invites-accept-all.spec.ts` against a local Tuwunel: four Primary invites (two DMs), Accept All, then all four joined and `m.direct` holds both DMs (matrix-js-sdk 41.7's `setAccountData` resolves after the sync echo, so the second write reads the first).
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings), Prettier, the inbox and i18n unit tests (124), and the e2e spec in Chromium.
- Independent review (subagent): changes required for a mid-batch decline being re-joined (fixed by the skip above), with nits on the unit test not pinning the join order, a single DM in the e2e, and the order comment; all fixed.
  CodeRabbit (PR #461): card Accept and Decline stayed enabled during the batch, so a card's DM accept could race the batch's `m.direct` write; they are now disabled while it runs.
  PR #461 dual review, round 1 at `5051866b`: Opus approved; Astra required changes because the card lock lives in the mounted list, so a tab switch mid-batch or a card Accept followed by Accept All could overlap two DM `m.direct` updates and lose one. Fixed at the `m.direct` helpers (the queue above) rather than with batch state that survives remounts; overlapping joins are harmless, as joining an already-joined room is a no-op. Opus's note that the Runbook overstated the card lock is fixed.
  Round 2 at `12a1125f`: both required changes for the queue being module-global, so after an account switch the stopped client's pending write (no sync echo) held every `m.direct` update on the new account until reload; the queue is now a `WeakMap` keyed by client, with a regression test.
  Round 3 at `1ebec7dd`: Opus and Astra approved. Accepted from Opus: after a tab switch mid-batch, a card Decline whose leave has not synced when the batch reaches that room is joined again (invite-only rooms reject it); a decline on another device has the same window.
  Accepted: a 429 on the `m.direct` write after a successful join retries the whole accept, which then sees a joined room and leaves the DM untagged, as a failed write on the single-card path already does.

### Make the background jobs bar match the typing bar (2026-10-14)

- Why: the owner found the jobs bar from #446 out of place under "Mind is typing…": taller, larger text, one job's name shown twice ("Running: deep_research" and a `deep_research ✕` chip), and a ✕ that looked like the typing bar's harmless dismiss but stopped the job. A first pass (chips on a second row, glass ✕ and Stop all) still felt messy to the owner, who pointed at [Impeccable](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable): its distill and layout guidance (no nested containers, one control vocabulary, group by alignment instead of boxes) and `docs/ui-design.md` ("let the enclosing surface own the glass; avoid stacking opaque fills, rims, or blur on every child") both ruled out bordered chips holding glass circle buttons inside a glass bar.
- Change (`BackgroundJobsBar.tsx`, `backgroundJobsBar.css.ts`, `backgroundJobsPresentation.ts`): the bar keeps its own surface, spaced from the typing bar as `docs/ui-design.md` asks, at the typing bar's padding, `T200` text and 32px height. Inside it nothing has a fill, rim or border: Stop and Stop all are text buttons (Folds `Chip`, `fill="None"`) that show a fill only on hover. One job is one row, its title ("Running: deep_research") and Stop. Several jobs are a title row ("3 background jobs", Stop all) over a list (`ul`) of 24px rows aligned under the title's text: the job's name, then a muted "Waiting for approval" or "Stopping…" (which ends where a Stop's text does), then Stop, so names and actions each form one column. Row Stops are regular weight under the bar's own Stop or Stop all, and on touch screens rows are 2.5rem tall so adjacent Stops stand apart. The list keeps room for a focus ring inside its scroll box, states `role="list"` (WebKit drops a bullet-less list's role), sizes its indent and rows in rem so page zoom keeps them aligned, and Stop keeps an edge in forced colors. The rows' status replaces the "Waiting for approval: shell" label (`waiting`, new, in place of each item's `label`). The job control's label is "Stop {tool}" (`stopJob`, replacing `cancel`) and its error "Could not stop {tool}" (`stopFailed`, replacing `cancelFailed`), so Stop, Stop all and Stopping… share one verb; `stop` is new, and Dutch "Stopping…" reads "Wordt gestopt…", not the same word as Stop. Strings are in every locale. One job's Stop and several jobs' Stop all are different buttons, so a focused Stop never becomes Stop all; when a focused control goes (a job ending, two jobs becoming one, or one becoming two), focus stays on the bar, but not after the person moved focus to the page or another window (a blur without a new target whose control is still in the document).
- Several jobs then fold into one line, at the owner's request: "3 background jobs ⌃ … Stop all". A mouse resting on the title for 150ms lists the jobs, and leaving the bar closes them; the rest of the bar (Stop all) and a pointer passing over on its way to the composer or the bars above do not open them, so no Stop opens under a pointer headed for the typing bar's ✕ or the approval bar's Review. Pressing the title (a disclosure button with `aria-expanded`), by click, tap or Enter, keeps them listed until it is pressed again, Escape, a press outside, or focus leaving the bar; focus moving into the list keeps them listed too, so a keyboard user is not dropped when the mouse leaves. Escape with focus in the bar returns it to the title and goes no further (the room otherwise sends Escape to the composer, `MindroomRoomView.tsx`); elsewhere it closes the list and goes on. Hover is mouse-only, so a tap does not open and close at once, as in `MindroomThreadSummaryMarker`, whose click-pins-a-hovered-list behavior this keeps. The list shows above the title row, so the title and Stop all stay under the pointer, but follows the title in the DOM (CSS grid areas), so Tab and screen readers reach the jobs before Stop all. While listed, the bar takes the approval review's dense tint (`glassDenseOverBackdrop`), so the typing bar behind does not show through the rows. The title's hit area spans the bar's height; only the title text is a live region. While listed, the bar's place in the footer (`Anchor`) keeps its one-line height and the bar grows over the timeline: the footer's height feeds `--room-footer-height` and re-pins the timeline (`MindroomRoomTimeline.tsx`), so growing the footer would move the timeline on every hover. An open list covers Jump to Latest and Show less above the footer, as a menu would, without changing the footer inset; pressing there lands on the list.
- Tests: `BackgroundJobsBar.test.tsx` adds one job shown in the title with Stop and no list; focus staying in the bar when two jobs become one and one becomes two, and when one job is replaced by another; focus left where the person moved it (each fails without its fix); a row saying a job waits for approval until it is stopping; several jobs on one line, listed while the title is pressed (a mouse leaving does not close them then); Escape in the bar closing the list back on the title without reaching the room's Escape, Escape elsewhere, the title and a press outside closing it; a mouse resting 150ms on the title listing them, but not one on Stop all, one passing over the title, or a touch, and a press inside keeping them; and focus in the list keeping them listed when the mouse leaves, and focus leaving the bar closing them; a bar that went away with focus in it not taking focus for a later job (each fails without its behavior); the one-job stopping cases check the title; the other cases use the new labels. `backgroundJobsPresentation.test.ts` checks `waiting` and the names instead of labels. `e2e/background-jobs-bar.spec.ts` uses the new button names and checks the status in the `shell` row; it checks that a mouse resting on the title lists three jobs without changing the footer's height, that leaving closes them, that Tab after Enter on the title reaches the first job's Stop before Stop all and Escape returns to the title, and that pressing the title (also on a phone) keeps them listed, and captures the collapsed bar and a phone's listed jobs.
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings), Prettier, the background-jobs and i18n unit tests (148), and `e2e/background-jobs-bar.spec.ts` against a local Tuwunel pass. A temporary spec (not committed) captured the composer footer with Mind typing, before and after, in Chromium, light and dark, desktop and phone width, with one job, three (one waiting, one stopping) collapsed, listed by a resting mouse and by Enter, a long name waiting for approval on a phone, hover, and keyboard focus: the typing and jobs bars measure 32px each with one job (the jobs bar was about 46px), and fifteen jobs scroll inside the bar with Stop all in view.
- Independent review (subagent) of the first pass: changes required for focus lost when two jobs became one; fixed, with its nits on the error string, the Dutch "Stopping…", RTL padding, the error's text size, stale comments, and tests that matched `stoppingJob` as a prefix. Its design flags (a ✕ like the typing bar's, two chip styles in one bar) went with the chips in the second pass.
- PR #460 dual review, round 1 at `27291b23`: Astra approved; Opus required changes for focus restoration surviving the bar's unmount, so stopping the last job and a later job arriving pulled focus into the bar; the flag now clears when the bar renders nothing. Also from Opus, as over-engineering: Escape in the bar is a React handler on `Anchor` instead of a native listener, and the list's fade and the chevron's transition are gone as unrequested polish (the chevron still flips). Declined: the title's live region remounting when one job becomes two, which can skip that one announcement; the previous review asked to keep the button out of the live region.
- Independent review (subagent) of the hover version: changes required for hover opening from anywhere on the bar, putting Stops over the typing bar's ✕ and the approval bar's Review, and for Tab reaching Stop all before the listed jobs; both fixed, with its nits on an untested hover delay and close paths, a keyboard user dropped when the mouse left, a fractional footer height, Escape handled with the composer's, motion tokens, text showing through the open list, the title's touch target, an unasserted phone tap, and a button inside the live region. Declined: a click on a hover-opened title closing it (it pins, as `MindroomThreadSummaryMarker` does). Not covered: WebKit (the main Playwright config runs Chromium only).
- Independent review (subagent) of the second pass: changes required for "Stopping…" ending past the Stop column and focus rings clipped by the scrolling list; fixed, with its nits on long names vanishing beside the status, zoom, list semantics, the Stop column's weight, the muted text (now `P300`, as the approval bar's detail), focus when one job is replaced by another, a blur to the page pulling focus back later (already in the first pass), forced colors, touch spacing, and tests. Declined: the list's Stops moving left of Stop all by a classic scrollbar's width past six jobs; repeated `Chip` props in the two buttons.

### Recover sessions rejected by Tuwunel's refresh endpoint (2026-10-13)

- Why: Brave showed the homeserver connectivity dialog while Matrix requests returned `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` and `/refresh` returned `403 M_FORBIDDEN` with "Refresh token is unrecognized."
  `createSessionTokenRefresh` treated only `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` as a definitive rejection, so the SDK retried the unusable session instead of emitting `Session.logged_out`.
- Change: refresh errors with `M_FORBIDDEN` now follow the same SDK logout policy as `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`.
  Existing session-aware cleanup returns the user to sign-in; network failures, rate limits, and server failures remain retryable.
  The Connect page shares the refresh function: `requestAsStoredSession` maps `TokenRefreshLogoutError` to `HomeserverSignedOutError`, so an `M_FORBIDDEN` refresh there now shows "This account needs to sign in again before it can approve." with a "Sign in to approve" button instead of the raw `MatrixError: [403] …` refresh error with Approve disabled.
- Race: without Web Locks, two tabs can spend the same refresh token; the loser now re-checks storage after a failed refresh and adopts the winner's stored rotation instead of logging out.
  Accepted limit: a rejection that lands before the winner stores its rotation still logs out, as `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` already did.
  Current servers don't send `M_FORBIDDEN` there: Tuwunel (since 2026-06) re-issues within a grace window or returns `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` for a replay, and Synapse rejects a reused token with `M_FORBIDDEN` only after the rotated token was used, so after the winner stored it (its other `M_FORBIDDEN` refresh errors are true expiries).
- Tests: both rejection codes are covered directly and through the real Matrix SDK request/refresh/logout flow, with rate-limit and server-failure controls.
  The two `M_FORBIDDEN` regressions and the race regression fail before their fixes.
- Independent review: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; round 1 found the no-Web-Locks race above. The startup logout listener attaches before `startClient`.
- Validation: all 6,736 tests pass under Node 24 on Linux, including 76 focused refresh/startup/cleanup tests also passing locally.
  Linux typecheck and lint pass (0 errors, 18 existing warnings); the production build passes under Node 24 on a temporary case-sensitive macOS volume.
  The macOS case-sensitive volume avoided the `ApprovalArgumentFields` casing collision that #457 since fixed.

### Fold people's long messages and show agent replies in full, as T3 Code does (2026-10-12)

- Why: the owner asked for T3 Code's behavior, where a long pasted or typed message shows folded once it is sent.
  T3 Code (`MessagesTimeline.tsx`, `CollapsibleUserMessageBody`) folds user messages over 600 characters or 8 lines to an 11rem preview with a bottom fade and "Show full message" / "Show less"; agent replies never fold by length, and there is no setting.
  This client folds the same way (an `11em` cap measured by height, a fade, the same labels), but its account switch "Expand long messages by default" has been on by default since 2026-09-13 (`7842a0d5`), so nothing folded, a long paste included.
- Change:
  - The switch (`expandLongMessagesByDefault` in `io.mindroom.settings`, its Settings row, and its strings in all 17 locales) is gone; a stored value is ignored. Every timeline starts folded, and `[+all]` / `[-all]` remain the per-timeline override.
  - Agent replies (`isMindroomAgentUserId`, a `mindroom_` localpart) use `always-expanded`: they never fold and have no toggle. Detection is by sender only, not by MindRoom metadata, so metadata arriving with a streamed edit cannot flip a row's mode mid-life.
  - People's messages, the viewer's included, fold past `11em` as before.
  - Forced overflow (folding without measuring) counts only the plain `body` length: link- and table-heavy HTML passed the 1200-character check while rendering short, and a forced row is never measured, so it folded with nothing hidden.
  - `[+all]` / `[-all]` keep the reader's place. The button broadcast `expandAllMessages()` / `collapseAllMessages()` to every mounted row in the same click that changed the baseline, and React 18 batched both into one commit, so `useTimelineBulkExpansionAnchor` captured its anchor after the rows had already resized and the reader's message moved off screen (it did on `dev` too; only the removed switch changed the baseline alone). The button now sets only the timeline's baseline, and rows follow it through `ExpandAllInitContext` one commit later, as they did for the switch. The broadcast, which also reached rows in other open timelines, is gone.
  - The viewer's own messages no longer use live expand-once. That policy (`getLiveCollapsibleMessageExpandId`) opens a long message once as it arrives live, and took own messages too; with agent replies always in full, it now applies only to other people. In a thread, the local echo fires no `Room.timeline` (the main timeline rejects thread events); the server's echo fires it with `liveEvent: true` under the real `$` ID, which marked the row `initially-expanded` and opened it for good. In the room view, the local echo fires live under its `~` transaction ID and was marked too, but rows are keyed by event ID, so the row remounted under its `$` ID and folded. `shouldTrackLiveCollapsibleMessage` now skips events from `room.myUserId`, covering sends and edits from any of the viewer's devices.
- Decision history: PR #449 first grew a three-way setting (Auto, On, Off) with a `30em` fold for agent replies; both reviewers approved it, and the owner then dropped it as over-engineered in favor of T3 Code's behavior with no setting.
- Tests:

With the broadcast restored and a pointer click, the reader's message is lost after `[+all]`; without it, the anchor holds.
