### Swipe a compact card to resolve or reopen its thread (2026-10-12)

- Why: on phones and tablets the compact room view hides the hover Resolve button (`CardQuickAction` is `display: none` under `(max-width: 480px), (hover: none)`), so resolving took the ⋯ menu and a second tap. The owner asked for an iOS-style swipe.
- Change: `CompactCardSwipe` wraps each compact card and its action buttons. A touch that moves toward the inline start (left, or right in RTL layouts) slides the card with the finger over a strip that reads Resolve (or Reopen thread for a resolved card). The card moves from where the touch locked sideways, so it does not jump by the lock distance. The strip turns solid (success green, or the primary color for reopen) once the card has travelled `clamp(35% of its width, 72px, 160px)`; letting go there toggles the thread through the same `setResolved` as the menu, anything shorter springs back. The strip's label and color are taken when the swipe starts and kept while the card settles, so a committed resolve does not relabel it Reopen thread mid-animation. Only touch pointers swipe: mouse and keyboard keep the hover buttons and the menu. The track sets `touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom`, so vertical scrolling stays native, and a gesture whose first 10px are mostly vertical is left to the scroller. Once a touch is a sideways swipe, a native non-passive `touchmove` listener cancels it, as `useEdgeSwipe` does, in case iOS would otherwise start a vertical pan when the swipe drifts. Width and direction are read when the swipe locks, not on every touch. Touches that start within 28px of a screen edge (`EDGE_START_MAX_X`, now exported by `useEdgeSwipe`) go to the edge swipes for back and forward. The click that can follow a swipe is swallowed so the card does not also open; keyboard clicks (`detail` 0) pass. A `lostpointercapture` on the track ends the swipe without acting: a live re-sort that moves the row drops the capture, and later events would go to another card, leaving this one stuck mid-swipe. The same event bubbling from the card button, when the touch's implicit capture moves to the track, is ignored (without that check every swipe ends at once in Chromium). Settling ends on the track's own `transform` `transitionend`, with a 500ms fallback for a cancelled transition. The swipe is off for pinned threads (they cannot be resolved), unsent local-echo roots (`setResolved` throws for them), readers without the thread-tags permission, and a thread whose tag update is pending; it is also dropped if the card turns disabled mid-swipe. Letting go acts on the state the swipe started from (`onSwipe(wasResolved)`), so if another client toggles the thread mid-swipe the action still matches the strip.
- The card's DOM gains one wrapper (`[data-compact-card-swipe="track"]`) between `CardShell` and the card; the action buttons sit inside it so they move with the card. The e2e fixture uses the same wrapper.
- Known limits: no haptic tick when the strip arms (`@capacitor/haptics` is installed but unused). No partial-swipe "reveal and tap" state as in iOS Mail; the swipe acts on release or springs back. Touches in the 28px edge zones do not swipe cards.
- Tests: `CompactCardSwipe.test.tsx` (20 cases) covers commit, spring-back, arming from the lock point, the strip hiding after the track's own settle transition and after the fallback, the strip keeping its label through the settle, acting on the swipe-start state when the thread toggles mid-swipe, vertical drags, the `touchmove` guard, the wrong direction, edge starts on both sides, mouse drags, a second finger, disabled and disabled-mid-swipe, `pointercancel`, lost capture (and the button's bubbled one), click swallowing with keyboard clicks passing, RTL and the reopen label. Each of 24 guard mutations (one condition removed or inverted at a time) fails at least one case. `CompactRoomView.test.ts`: a swipe resolves an open card and reopens a resolved one without opening either, and the swipe is off for pins, local-echo roots, readers and pending updates. `e2e/compact-thread-cards.spec.ts` drives CDP touch events in Chromium at 390px: a short swipe springs back, an edge start does nothing, a full swipe arms the strip and resolves without opening, a second swipe reopens, a vertical drag still scrolls, and a tap still opens.
- Independent review (subagent), round 1: required handling `lostpointercapture` (fixed, with the target check its suggested one-liner lacked; the e2e swipe fails without it). Also fixed from its notes: the strip could stay mounted when the settle transition was cancelled, a stale swipe flag could swallow a later keyboard click, the iOS vertical-pan guard, layout reads on every touch, the 10px jump at lock, the strip turning grey on a committed swipe, and guards without a test.
- PR #448 dual review, round 2 at `25680a83`: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra both approved with no changes requested. Left as is: the hover Resolve button still lacks the local-echo check (older than this PR), and a confirmed root that is not loaded can still reach `setResolved`'s logged throw (the swipe springs back; not worth the menu's per-render lookup).
- PR #448 dual review, round 1 at `a175cb34`: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra both approved (Astra's read-only sandbox could not run vitest). Fixed two of Opus's non-blocking notes: the strip could say Resolve while letting go reopened a thread another client resolved mid-swipe, and phones could now swipe unsent local-echo cards into a thrown `setResolved` (the hover button already could; gated on `isConfirmedMatrixEventId`, without the menu's per-render root lookup). Declined: resetting a swipe that never got an end event when a new touch starts (Opus judged it theoretical: lost capture reaches the track, since React's moves do not leave it detached).
- Independent review, round 2: confirmed the lost-capture target check. Fixed its blocker, `CompactRoomView.test.ts`'s node mock lacking `addEventListener` for the new track listener (4 scroll-restore cases failed); dropped a redundant settling check and tested the `cancelable` guard. Declined: a swipe started while the card is still springing back jumps from the animated position to the finger (cosmetic, rare).
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings) and Prettier pass. `npm test`: the known `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` (1) failures only. `npx playwright test e2e/compact-thread-cards.spec.ts` passes in Chromium. Armed Resolve and Reopen strips checked in light and dark themes in Chromium against `docs/ui-design.md` (Folds tokens, motion tokens, pointer moves not driving renders); WebKit could not be driven.
- Next: check on an iPhone (WebKit was not driven; Playwright's WebKit cannot send touch moves); consider a haptic tick on arming.

### Show MindRoom background jobs above the composer, with cancel (2026-10-11)

- Why: MindRoom PR #2113 lets a tool call, a subagent, or a gated call waiting for approval keep running after the reply that started it, as a job of its conversation. People need to see those jobs and cancel them at any time, since 🛑 now stops only the reply.
- Contract: each agent publishes its live jobs as the room state event `io.mindroom.background_jobs`, keyed by its own user ID: `{"jobs": [{"job_id", "thread_id", "kind", "tool", "status", "requester_id", "started_at"}]}`, with no arguments or results. `status` is `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `cancel_requested`. A client cancels with the room event `io.mindroom.background_job_cancel` (`{"job_id": ...}` or `{"all": true}`), in the thread when the view is a thread.
- Change (`src/app/mindroom/background-jobs/`): `backgroundJobsContract.ts` parses the state, accepting only events whose state key is their sender, from MindRoom agents still joined to the room. `useRoomBackgroundJobs` listens on the room for jobs events, agents' membership changes and a replaced live state only, so room rows do not re-render for unrelated state; an agent whose membership is not loaded yet (lazy-loaded members) counts as joined until its member event says otherwise, so only an agent known to have left has its last list ignored. A thread view shows its thread's jobs and the main timeline shows every job in the room. `BackgroundJobsBar` sits above the composer in `MindroomRoomView`: a title ("Running: run_tests", "Waiting for approval: shell", "Stopping: run_tests" once its cancel is sent here or elsewhere, or "3 background jobs"), one chip with ✕ per job (a job waiting for approval says so when there are several), and Stop all when there are several; Stop all sends one event, which every agent handles. A cancelled job shows "Stopping…" until it leaves the room's published jobs, also when it was cancelled elsewhere (`cancel_requested`), across a switch to another thread, and after the bar was unmounted (`sentCancels.ts` keeps each room's sent cancels outside the bar); pressing ✕ moves keyboard focus to the next ✕, and Stop all to the bar; a failed send restores a ✕ only when no other cancel reached that job, and its error shows only while one of its jobs is listed and not stopping here or elsewhere. A viewer whose power level does not allow `io.mindroom.background_job_cancel` sees the jobs without ✕ or Stop all. A long tool name is cut short in its chip and in the title (the full text is the title attribute) so the ✕ stays in view, and many jobs scroll inside the bar with Stop all outside the list. `RoomNavItem` shows a clock icon on a room with jobs, named "Background jobs running" in a hover tooltip since the clock also marks schedules; the clock stays while the row is hovered, like the live-call badge, so the tooltip can open. Agent call rooms give `io.mindroom.background_jobs` power level 0 so the agent can publish its jobs there, and an older call room gains it, with its other levels unchanged, before the next call starts in it. A subagent job reads "research (subagent)", named by the agent it runs. Strings are in every locale.
- Tests: `backgroundJobsContract.test.ts` (each listed job parsed with its agent; state whose key is not its sender, a non-agent sender, and an agent that left the room ignored; malformed items dropped; a missing thread maps to the main timeline; a thread sees only its jobs and the main timeline every job). `backgroundJobsPresentation.test.ts` (nothing without jobs; one running job, one waiting for approval, several in order; a requested cancel marks the item stopping; an approval-waiting job among several is labelled; subagent and unknown-kind labels). `cancelBackgroundJob.test.ts` (one job in its thread; every job from the main timeline with one event; a cancel that fails to send leaves no local echo to resend). `BackgroundJobsBar.test.tsx` (nothing without jobs; ✕ shows Stopping… while the job is still listed and until it leaves; a job cancelled elsewhere shows Stopping… without buttons; a failed send restores the ✕ and shows the error; a failed Stop all says the jobs could not be stopped; a failed Stop all keeps an earlier sent cancel stopping, and a job Stop all reached stays stopping without an error when its own earlier cancel then fails; a viewer who may not cancel gets no buttons; a cancel stays stopping across a thread switch; a failed cancel's error goes once its job is no longer listed, and once it is cancelled from elsewhere, and a later failure for a job that ended keeps a listed job's error; Stop all sends one event and marks every job stopping). `useRoomBackgroundJobs.test.tsx`, with a real `Room`: the jobs follow a live-timeline reset, an agent whose membership is not loaded shows until its leave arrives, and unrelated state causes no render. `RoomNavItem.test.tsx` (the room is marked while it has jobs). The RoomView tests mock the bar, as they mock the approval queue. `e2e/background-jobs-bar.spec.ts` (needs `E2E_UI_ACTIONS_HOMESERVER`): two agents publish four jobs over a real homeserver; the room list marks the room, the thread shows its three, ✕ sends the cancel event in the thread, `cancel_requested` (also for a job cancelled elsewhere) and removal update the bar, the main timeline shows all four, at phone width a long tool name keeps its ✕ on screen, alone or among fifteen jobs, and fifteen jobs keep the bar under half the screen with Stop all in view, and the bar goes when the jobs end; it captures desktop and phone screenshots in light and dark.
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings) pass, and the changed files pass Prettier (`prettier --check .` also flags 111 files this branch does not touch). `npm test`: 6,684 passed; the known `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` (1) cases fail the same way on this base, and `RoomTimeline.ledgerLifecycle.test.ts` timed out once under load and passes alone. The e2e spec passes against a local Tuwunel.
- PR #446 three-model review, round 1 at `74820fed` (Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra; all changes required). Fixed: lazy-loaded agent members hiding jobs (Opus), room rows re-rendering for every state event (all three), a failed Stop all erasing an earlier sent cancel and a thread switch dropping a cancel's mark (Sol), a stale cancel error under unrelated jobs (Opus), unused `requesterId`/`agentId` fields, CSS copied from the approval bar, the Arabic count form, and the key names (`running`, `awaitingApproval`, `jobCount`). Declined: the subscription going stale after a gappy sync (Opus, Astra): this fork's matrix-js-sdk patch makes `resetLiveTimeline` keep the live `RoomState` (`forkLive`), and the probes ran against an unpatched `node_modules`; the hook test covers a reset with the patched SDK, and the hook also refreshes on `CurrentStateUpdated`. ### Open the Connections portal signed in from settings (2026-10-09)

- Why: the owner wants the people who talk to their agents to connect their own OAuth accounts, such as Google or GitHub, in the MindRoom backend's Connections portal without dashboard access or an identity gateway in front of the API.
  The portal could only be entered through trusted-upstream JWT auth.
  A signed-in Chat user now opens it from Settings, General, and lands there signed in as their Matrix user.
- Design: a `postMessage` handoff, not a token in the URL.
  - The new "Connections" card renders right after the Computers card in `MindroomInterfaceSettings` (`settings/MindroomConnectionsSettings.tsx`).
    Its **Open Connections** button calls `openConnectionsPortal` (`connections/openConnections.ts`) synchronously from the click handler, with no `await` before it, so popup blockers allow the window.
  - The helper opens `<backend>/connections/` in the named window `mindroom-connections` without `noopener`, because the portal needs `window.opener` to ask for the token.
  - The portal posts `{ type: "mindroom:connections-ready" }` to its opener.
    Chat answers only when `event.source` is the window it opened and `event.origin` is the backend origin, and only for that message type.
  - Chat then requests a fresh Matrix OpenID token bound to the backend origin (the helper passes the origin it answers at to the card's token getter, which calls `requestAudienceOpenIdToken(mx, audience)`; once per ready message, never cached) and posts `{ type: "mindroom:connections-openid", openid_token }` with the backend origin as the target origin, so the browser drops the message if the window navigated elsewhere.
    A portal reload after its session expired asks again and gets a new token.
    A rejected token request sends nothing.
  - Chat stops listening when the window closes (polled once per second), and a second click replaces the first session instead of adding a second listener.
  - A token reply still pending when its portal session ends, by window close or a newer click, is dropped (commit `188ad5c4`), so it never reaches a window another account may now own.
  - Chat switches accounts without reloading the page, so the portal session outlives the old client, whose access token stays valid.
    The card's token getter therefore rejects when `mx.clientRunning` is false, both before requesting the token and after it resolves.
    A rejection makes `openConnections.ts` skip the reply, so after an account switch the portal reload shows its "Open Connections from MindRoom Chat" message instead of the old account.
  - The backend origin is the Computers service URL (`useComputerApiUrl()`), so a URL saved under Computers or the deployment default applies, and a service turned off there disables the card's button.
  - The card is hidden on native builds (`Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`), because the shells have no pop-up window to hand a token to.
  - When `window.open` returns `null`, the card shows "Your browser blocked the Connections window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.", and the message clears after a later click opens the window.
  - With no backend URL configured, the button is disabled and the card says "Set your MindRoom server under Computers to use Connections."
- Audience binding (follow-up): `requestAudienceOpenIdToken(mx, audience)` in `matrix/openidAudience.ts` posts `{"io.mindroom.audience": audience}` to `/user/{userId}/openid/request_token` through `mx.http.authedRequest`, the request `mx.getOpenIdToken()` makes with an empty body.
  The point is that a backend operator cannot replay the token against another deployment on the same homeserver, but only when the homeserver enforces the audience (MindRoom's Tuwunel fork with `mindroom_openid_audience` on).
  Stock homeservers, and the fork with the option off, ignore the field and issue unbound tokens that remain replayable within their lifetime.
  The Connections card uses the backend origin as the audience.
  The Computers panel (`ComputerPanel.tsx`, session creation) uses it too, with the origin of the computer service it posts to.
  The Element Call widget driver, Local MindRoom provisioning and the welcome page keep unbound `getOpenIdToken()` tokens on purpose.
  - Dependency: the Tuwunel fork's `io.mindroom.openid_audience` capability (`unstable_features` in `/_matrix/client/versions`), which stores the audience with the token and enforces it in federation `openid/userinfo`.
    Stock homeservers ignore the field and return an unbound token, which the backend accepts only when the homeserver lacks that capability.
    Roll out in this order: first MindRoom backends with audience support (mindroom-ai/mindroom#2775), then Chat including the iOS app (it only adds a body field that stock homeservers ignore), and turning on `mindroom_openid_audience` in Tuwunel (from v1.9.3-mindroom.28) last.
    The iOS app update must be live before the option is turned on, because older clients send unbound tokens that new backends reject with 401 once binding is on.
    Released backends verify Computers OpenID tokens without an audience (since v2026.9.147), so once the homeserver binds tokens and Chat requests them, those older backends reject the bound Computers tokens with 401.
- Backend dependency: mindroom-ai/mindroom#2775, which adds `POST /api/connections/session` (exchanges the token for a portal-only session cookie) and `MINDROOM_CONNECTIONS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
  That variable is a JSON list of exact Chat origins and must list the Chat origin that opens the portal, for example `["https://chat.mindroom.chat","https://chat.lab.mindroom.chat"]`, or the backend answers 403.
  The backend also needs `MINDROOM_CONNECTIONS_AGENT` set and a public HTTPS origin.
  Without the backend change the portal cannot sign the user in, so ship the two together.
- New keys in all 17 catalogs: `settings.general.connections.{sectionTitle,title,description,open,noBackend,blocked}`.
  Each catalog names the Computers section with its own `settings.general.computers.sectionTitle` word.
- Known limits: native (Capacitor) builds are not supported.
  The card needs the Computers backend URL, so a backend that serves Connections from another origin than Computers cannot be targeted separately.
  If the opened window navigates cross-origin but stays open, the listener lives until it closes, and its messages fail the source and origin checks.
- Tests: `openConnections.test.ts` covers the synchronous open, a blocked window, the source, origin and type checks, the exact target origin, a fresh token per ready message, a failed token request, polling, cleanup after close and a reopened window.
  Follow-up tests cover a token reply dropped when its session ends while the request is pending, by window close or a newer click.
  `MindroomConnectionsSettings.test.tsx` covers the native build rendering nothing, the disabled button with the `noBackend` text when no server is set or Computers is turned off, the portal opening with the deployment and the saved Computers URL, the token getter passed to the helper, and the blocked message appearing and clearing.
  It also covers no token being handed out after the Matrix client stopped (the SDK is not called), and a token that resolves after the client stopped being dropped.
  Mutation checks failed the matching tests: an `await` before the open, no native check, no `disabled`, and ignoring a blocked result.
  `matrix/openidAudience.test.ts` covers the exact path, method and body of the audience request and a failed request reaching the caller.
  The helper test checks that the token getter receives the same backend origin the reply is posted to, the card test that the request carries the audience it is given, and `ComputerPanel.test.tsx` that the panel passes its computer service origin.
  `i18n.test.ts` confirms every catalog has the keys.
- Validation: typecheck and ESLint (0 errors, 18 existing warnings, none in the new files) pass, and Prettier is clean on the changed files.
  `npm test`: everything passes except `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and one `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` case, which fail the same way on `dev`; rerun after merging `dev` on 2026-10-16.
  Not run live: the handshake against a real backend with `POST /api/connections/session` has not run yet.
  The PR's screenshots render the card on a standalone page with a demo client, and the portal with live lab assets and demo API data.
- PR #442 three-model review, round 1 at `e3e71c76`: Sol and Astra approved; Opus required changes for the token audience and the target origin being derived in two places (the helper now passes its backend origin to the token getter, and the Computers panel uses its service origin as is), and for stale validation notes here and in the PR body.
- PR #442 three-model review, round 2 at `76ea54be`: Sol and Astra approved; Opus required dropping the token request's own catch, since the call site already swallows a failed request.

### Evict whole unused rooms when media cannot bring the cache under budget (2026-10-09)

- Why: an iPhone diagnostics export showed cache eviction running at every app start and again before each suspension, which only happens over the 1 GiB budget, and no gap-fill or history page in 11 hours. Since #298, eviction deleted optional media only ("text, essential bodies and pinned rooms survive pressure"), while the budget counts text and essential bodies too. Once those alone exceeded it, `canSavePage` refused every room's gap pages, history pages and downloads for good, and nothing but a manual Clear could lower the total. The owner chose to evict text from rooms nobody is using rather than exempt the focused room's gap. This restores the room eviction the original D9 design had (#298 replaced it).
- Change (`cacheEviction.ts`): optional media goes first, as before. When that is not enough, whole rooms go through `clearRoomCachedContent` (events of every scope, meta and markers, thread summaries, attachment references and unshared blobs, the ledger row) until the total is back under 90% of the budget. Each clear returns the bytes it freed (the ledger row's total and the unshared blobs' sizes from their references, including references marked missing), and the stores are re-read only once that estimate meets the target, instead of a key cursor over every attachment after each room. Rooms known only from attachment references (their last event was deleted, which drops the ledger row) are candidates too, first. Before each room the pass reads its pin and recent-open stamp from the stores and then checks the focus and download registries, in that order, so nothing awaits between the last check and the clear revoking the room's writes; focus and download are also checked before each media deletion. A pass can take seconds, and the user may open, leave, download or pin a room meanwhile. When protected rooms alone exceed the budget (their text plus every blob a protected room references, computed in the media phase), no room is cleared: that cannot end the pressure and would empty the other rooms on every pass. `clearRoomCachedContent` now removes events with one key-range delete instead of a cursor that deserialized every event while locking all six stores; Clear gets the same. Order is least recently opened first (rooms never opened before any), then least recent activity. D9 put federated rooms first, but the federated flag is stamped only when a room is focused, and activity measures traffic, not use, so both evicted rooms the user reads before rooms nobody opened. Protected, as for media: the focused room, rooms opened in the last 24 hours, pinned rooms, and now rooms with an explicit Download running (`setEvictionDownloadingRoomIds`, kept per session by the offline controller and rebuilt when it starts again), which their own save check would otherwise evict mid-download. Pressure therefore remains only when protected rooms alone exceed the budget, which is what the "protected content fills the storage" pause already says.
- Concurrent checks share one pass per session (three ran at once at every start in the export, each taking about 6.6 s), so they cannot each evict a room. `noteRoomFocused` protects the room before starting its offline work, instead of relying on that work reaching an await first.
- A room evicted after this session warmed it saves its live tail again when focused (`evictedSinceWarm`, from the durable `opened` flag that eviction clears). On iOS a session can outlive the 24-hour protection.
- Diagnostics: each pass over budget records `storage.cache.eviction` in the deep trace (budget, bytes before and after, protected bytes, evicted media and room counts, whether pressure remains), so the next export shows whether protected rooms alone exceed the budget. Under lasting pressure every save check records one, which can crowd the trace's ring buffer.
- Known limits: a downloaded room that is not pinned and not opened for a day can be evicted; Pin keeps it. A pin written between the per-room check and that room's clear (milliseconds) is not seen. Writes in flight for an evicted room are revoked, so a busy room that is not open can start its new cache with an unmarked hole; the re-warm repairs it only within the same session. When protected data is between 90% of the budget and the budget, every pass empties all unprotected rooms (media already behaved this way). The focus and download registries live in one tab's memory and revocation cancels only that tab's writes, so a room left open in another tab for over a day can be evicted while that tab keeps writing to it (Clear already behaved this way). Open-thread seeds and offline snapshots held in memory for an evicted room stay until the room is opened or its panel refreshes, as with Clear. 
- Tests: `cacheEviction.test.ts`: rooms evict in LRU order with recent, focused and pinned rooms kept and markers removed; never-opened rooms go before rooms opened over a day ago, regardless of federation or traffic; a room focused while its stored protection is read is kept; a room opened and left during the pass is kept; unused rooms are left alone when protected text alone exceeds the budget, and when a protected room's media alone does (fails with a text-only total); an evicted room's attachment bytes count toward the target; a room focused during the pass is kept (fails without the per-room check); an evicted room's essential bodies go with it; protected rooms alone keep pressure and text, and the trace records the totals; concurrent checks share one pass and record one trace event; a room pinned during the pass is kept; a room known only from references is evicted; a room whose download starts during the media phase keeps its media; one session's download update does not unprotect another's; a five-room pass reads the attachment total three times, not once per room. `roomOfflineController.test.ts`: a running download keeps a cold room's cache under pressure (fails without the download protection) and the room is evicted once it is canceled; an evicted room's live tail is saved again on the next focus (fails without `evictedSinceWarm`); a finished download and a stopped engine release the protection (each fails without its release); a restarted engine protects a paused download again. `cacheStoreLifecycle.test.ts`'s failed-clear rollback now aborts on the events range delete instead of a cursor delete. The storage-pause-after-a-live-body case now opens its room first, since an unprotected room is evicted instead of paused. The new eviction cases fail on `dev`.
- PR #445 dual review, round 3 at `79d50e43`: Astra approved; Opus required changes for the media phase's owner map, which copied each MXC URI's list per reference. Every edited message without media has a reference with an empty MXC URI, so a cache with 50,000 edited agent replies spent about 9 s per pass building it (Node: 8.7 s before, 2.1 ms after). The map now skips empty URIs and appends in place, and `clearRoomCachedContent` reads blob sizes from one map instead of scanning the room's references per blob. Third round with a new defect: the owner chose to fix it and re-review rather than restructure.
- PR #445 dual review, round 2 at `2fd46580`: Astra approved; Opus required changes for the protected-overflow guard counting only text, so a focused room whose essential bodies fill the budget still emptied every other room on each pass. Fixed: the media phase returns the protected rooms' text plus every blob they reference, the guard and the trace (`protected_bytes`) use it. Also from Opus: the freed bytes now count blobs whose references are marked missing, and `noteRoomFocused`'s comment no longer says eviction favors federated rooms.
- PR #445 dual review, round 1 (Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, both changes required at `b6109e3a`): fixed focus and download being checked before awaiting the ledger read (both), a room opened and left during the pass losing its new recent-open protection (Astra), clearing every unprotected room when protected text alone exceeds the budget (Opus), the federated-and-traffic order evicting used rooms first (Opus), and an unused event count in `clearRoomCachedContent` (Opus); added a test for the attachment part of the freed bytes. Declined: removing `protectDownloads()` from `start()` (the engine API supports stop and start, and the protection must match the intents a restart resumes) and reverting the `noteRoomFocused` reorder (harmless, and it no longer relies on `run()` reaching an await first); several tabs are a known limit.
- PR #445 bot review (Qodo): fixed the download registry shared across sessions, pins and in-pass downloads not rechecked, rooms with references but no ledger row never considered, protection not rebuilt after a controller restart, and the total re-read after every room. New cases fail without each fix. Declined: stopping before every unprotected room is cleared when protected rooms hold 90% to 100% of the budget (only clearing them brings the total under budget; those rooms were not opened for a day; listed in known limits).
- Independent review (subagent): confirmed the root cause (budget made of ledger bytes and blobs, both now reclaimable except for protected rooms; no orphan essential blobs can be created; ledger drift heals when a row is deleted). Fixed: the protected set read once per pass (a room focused mid-pass was evicted), events deleted through a deserializing cursor, the shared-pass test only checking promise identity, untested federated order and protection release, and the focus ordering in `noteRoomFocused`. Declined: reusing the media phase's meta read (one extra read, only when rooms must go).
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings) and Prettier pass. `npm test`: 6,653 passed and 4 failed, the known `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` (1) cases, which fail the same way on `dev`. Not checked on a device yet.
- Next: after the next TestFlight build, export diagnostics and read `storage.cache.eviction` for the real totals; if protected rooms alone exceed the budget, revisit the 24-hour protection or the budget.

### Catch an open thread up after a sync gap, even when the room gap waits (2026-10-09)

- Why: on iOS, opening the app after about 40 minutes in the background left the thread on screen without the replies sent meanwhile until the owner left the thread and came back. The diagnostics export showed it at every long resume over 11 hours: the resume sync was limited (the SDK converted the thread's reset tokens), the server's reply count went from 699 to 701 while the thread kept rendering 699, and nothing fetched until the reopen, whose latest-slice refresh and reconcile showed 701.
- Cause: an open thread caught up after a sync gap only through the room gap fill (#281): a committed `/messages` page tells `useThreadGapRecovery`, which re-reads the thread cache. Since #298 that fill goes through the offline controller and pauses while the cache is over its byte budget, offline, hidden, or out of history allowance for the visit. The export shows no gap-fill or deep-history page in any session, and cache eviction ran at every app start and again before the suspension, which only happens over the 1 GiB budget. Eviction deletes attachments only, so it cannot bring event bytes under the budget, and `canSavePage` keeps refusing the room's gap pages. `RoomEvent.TimelineRefresh`, which already refreshes an open thread, is not what a limited sync emits.
- Fix (`useThreadGapRecovery`): a `RoomEvent.TimelineReset` on the room's unfiltered timeline set schedules one thread reconcile (newest `/relations` first, until it overlaps the thread cache), the pass every thread open runs, and appends its repaired events through the same loaded-span filter as cache recovery. It does not depend on the room gap fill or its policy. Resets that arrive during a pass coalesce into one more pass. A reconcile already running for the thread (an open's pass that began before the reset) is awaited first, since the scheduler would hand a duplicate request that pass's pre-gap result. The hook reads `append` and `getLoadedEvents` from a ref, updated after commit, at delivery time: `setSupplementalThreadEvents` changes identity when the SDK creates the thread, which the same limited sync can do, and re-running the effect discarded the pass in flight (the cache-read recovery had the same race). The pass logs to the thread trace (`thread.reconcile.*` in the diagnostics export) and warns on a rejection.
- Known limits: the room gap fill and the offline download stay paused while the cache is over its budget; the room timeline (no thread open) still waits for it, and a full cache never fills the gap behind a limited sync. A reconcile with a saved continuation (an earlier scan of a long thread that stopped short) scans that first and fetches the newest page only after it, so a continuation that hits the 25-page cap leaves the newest replies to the next pass. Each pass appends fresh cache copies of the thread's events, so every cached row the SDK does not hold is re-merged once per limited sync.
- Tests: `useThreadGapRecovery.test.tsx` gained three cases. With the cache over budget, a reset renders the missed reply from `/relations` and sends no `/messages` request (fails without the fix). A callback that changes identity during the pass still receives the reply (fails with the callbacks as effect dependencies). A pass that finishes after navigating to another thread neither renders its reply nor replaces the other thread's rows (fails without the `active` guard). The harness answers `/relations` separately and emits the reset on the room as well as the client, as the SDK does; the two in-flight cache-read cases emit on the client only, so their spy holds the gap-fill read (they fail again when `refresh` stops coalescing).
- PR #444 bot review: fixed Qodo's reset pass joining a thread-open pass that predates the gap (new case: an open's pass running at the reset, failing without the wait) and CodeRabbit's render-time ref update in the hook. Declined: moving `MindroomRoomTimeline`'s `loadedThreadEventsRef` out of render (the file assigns about twenty refs that way; out of scope here), and a newest-page-first reconcile for long threads with a saved continuation (Qodo; a known limit above, owned by `reconcilerScan`'s phase order, which the open path shares).
- Independent review (subagent): confirmed the SDK emits the room reset on the Room and the new case fails without the fix. Fixed its findings on the in-flight cases no longer guarding `refresh` after the harness change, the callback-identity race, the missing `.catch` and the untraced pass. Declined: also appending the cache page when nothing diverged (after the race fix the remaining case is a remount, which the open path covers, and it would re-merge every row on each reset), a newest-page-first reconcile mode, and avoiding the re-merge (both listed in known limits).
- Validation: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings) and Prettier pass. `npm test`: 6,626 passed and 4 failed, the known `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` (1) cases, which fail the same way on a clean checkout of this base. Not checked on a device yet.
- Next: decide how a cache over budget should treat the focused room's tail gap (exempt the first gap page from `canSavePage`, or evict cached events, not only attachments); add gap-fill outcomes to the diagnostics export, which has no record of a deferred fill.

### Hide stale link-preview scroll arrows (2026-10-09)

- Status: implemented and independently reviewed on `fix-url-preview-scroll-controls`, based on latest `dev`.
- Evidence: the reported arrow is the link-preview strip's forward control. The owner's Brave
  page had refreshed and received more messages before inspection, so the transient state was
  gone; no Safari-specific failure or individual preview request failure was confirmed live.
  The stale-arrow trigger was never reproduced: the old end-marker IntersectionObserver code
  recovered in every Chromium fixture tried (delayed/immediate failures, collapsed parent,
  display:none, offscreen, streaming URL churn, zoom). Only the empty strip's top margin was
  confirmed. This change is hardening that replaces the suspect mechanism, not a proven
  root-cause fix; if the arrow returns after previews work, look outside the holder.
- Fix: replace end-marker intersection state with measured horizontal overflow, observe both
  the viewport and content dimensions, and update after scrolling. Keep controls outside the
  measured content, with the back control before the cards in tab order as before. Failed
  cards leave no arrow or top margin, while mounted children remain able to recover on
  subsequent preview loads. Preserve right-to-left scrolling.
- Validation: focused tests pass (2 files / 10 tests), full `npm test` passes (695 files /
  6,634 tests with `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`), typecheck and production/PWA
  build pass. Touched-file ESLint and Prettier pass; full ESLint has the existing 18 warnings.
  Independent review approves overflow, lifecycle, geometry, and RTL behavior.
- Live: Brave fixture using the actual holder, folds styles, and theme confirms horizontal
  overflow, centered arrows, resize removal, RTL scrolling, and failed-card cleanup to zero
  height, zero top margin, and zero buttons. The fixture was removed after validation.
- Server cause (why no cards render): production `mindroom.chat` (`v1.9.3-mindroom.27`) has
  no URL-preview allowlist, so every preview gets 403 "URL is not allowed to be previewed".
  Dotfiles PR #115 sets `url_preview_domain_explicit_allowlist = ["*"]` in
  `configs/nixos/hosts/hetzner-matrix/tuwunel.nix` and keeps default IP filtering; its
  isolated test shows loopback, IPv4-mapped IPv6, and localhost previews never connect.
- Next: deploy client #443 and dotfiles #115, then refresh the browser to clear cached
  rejected preview requests.

### Reconnect the computer panel on its own after the server closes the stream (2026-10-09)

- Why: production logs showed the Computer panel dying whenever the server closed its stream (code 1008, which noVNC reports as a clean close).
  The server does that when a periodic re-authorization fails or times out, the worker restarts, the computer generation changes or the session expires, and it revokes the session at the same time, so the next status or stream-ticket call answers 401, sometimes 409 first ("Computer worker changed; create a new session.").
  The panel showed "Computer disconnected"; Reconnect reused the revoked session, so it took a second click after a 401 and never recovered from a 409.
  Session creation also failed hard on a cold worker: it takes 20 to 25 s after a scale to zero and up to about 3 minutes on a fresh node, and Cloudflare answers 524 after about 100 s.
- Status: merged in #440; review follow-ups on `fix/computer-recover-followups`; not deployed.
- Automatic reconnect (`ComputerPanel.tsx`, `reconnectAutomatically`): when a stream that had connected closes and no operation (take, Resume agent, Stop, Reconnect) is pending, the panel shows "Reconnecting to computer…" and retries after 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 s (about 15 s in all).
  Each attempt refreshes the status and fetches a new ticket for the same session.
  A stream opened by an attempt that closes before it connects uses the next attempt, and so does one that closes within 35 s of connecting; only a stream that stayed connected for 35 s gives the next close a full set again (`STABLE_STREAM_MS`).
  35 s outlasts the runtime's 15 s recheck cadence plus its 15 s budget, so a session revoked by every periodic recheck on a busy runtime also keeps counting.
  Without that, a server that revokes every new session right after it connects made the panel create sessions forever.
  After the last attempt, or on an error that is neither transient nor a revoked session, the panel shows "Computer disconnected" with the error and Reconnect, as before.
  Closing the panel, Stop, switching agent, room or thread, and Resume agent's own stream swap do not reconnect: they either clear the active stream first or are pending operations, and Resume keeps its `releasingStreamTicketRef` path.
- Revoked sessions: a 401, 404 or 409 from the existing session, during an automatic or a manual Reconnect, drops it (`replaceSession`: best-effort DELETE) and restarts the session effect, which creates a new session for the same room, thread and agent.
  `recoverOnRestartRef` tells that restart to show "Reconnecting…" and to keep counting attempts, so a session that is revoked again and again cannot loop forever.
  The server released control with the old session, so a user who had control comes back watching.
- A replacement session's first stream ticket goes through the same policy: a transient error or a revoked session on it uses the next automatic attempt instead of showing "Computer unavailable" (`reconnectAutomaticallyRef`).
- Starting: the session effect retries `POST /sessions` after network failures and 502, 503, 504 and 524, with delays of 2, 4, 8 and then 10 s, for up to 3 minutes from the first try, keeping the "Connecting…" spinner; a new OpenID token is fetched per try.
  The budget is checked again after each wait, so a throttled or sleeping tab that wakes after 3 minutes does not send another request.
  403, 409, 429 and every other status fail at once as before.
  While a session is being created the spinner adds "Starting the computer can take a minute."
- Cancellation: every wait goes through `wait(ms, signal)` on the session effect's `AbortSignal` (`lifecycleSignalRef`), and reconnect requests pass the same signal, so the effect cleanup (close, scope change, unmount) clears pending timers and aborts requests.
  A session created after the cleanup is disposed, as before.
- Known limits: a few 503s are configuration errors ("Computer authorization runtime is unavailable.", "A dedicated computer worker backend is required."), and the panel retries them for 3 minutes before showing them.
  When Cloudflare gives up with 524 the backend still finishes starting the worker; since mindroom#2773 the runtime revokes a session whose request disconnected, so the retry does not leave it holding one of the requester's eight sessions.
  Another viewer's Stop (or the same user's, in another tab) changes the computer's generation, so this panel gets 409 "Computer stopped or restarted; create a new session." and starts the computer again with a new session within a second.
  The server sends the same answer when the display or the agent's browser restarts, which should recover, so the client cannot tell the two apart; a distinct server answer for an explicit stop would fix it.
  Stop is disabled while the automatic attempts run (up to about 15 s), and the interaction stays locked, so an agent's request for another computer is refused meanwhile.
  A close while another operation is pending (Take control in flight, or Resume agent still sending its continuation) shows "Computer disconnected" as before, without reconnecting.
  The panel strings are still English only, like the rest of the panel.
- Tests (`ComputerPanel.test.tsx`, fake timers): reconnect after a close reusing a valid session; a full set of attempts again after a stream stayed connected; Reconnect after five attempts when every new session is revoked right after connecting (6 sessions, then none), when the new streams never connect, and at once on a 403 status; a 401 and a 409 during reconnect create a new session and come back in watch mode after control; exhausted attempts show Reconnect, which replaces a revoked session in one click; 503 then 524 on creation retries and connects; creation gives up after about 3 minutes; 403, 409 and 429 on creation do not retry; closing cancels a pending reconnect and a pending start retry (no timers left), and disposes a replacement session that arrives afterwards.
  Three existing cases changed: a 503 on creation is now retried, so the actionable-error case uses 403, 409 and 429; a close after a failed release, and a close after a failed continuation send, now reconnect on their own.
  The first round of new cases fails on `dev` (11 of them).
  Each of these mutations fails at least one case: dropping the pending-operation guard, the timer clearing on abort, 409 from the revoked statuses, the retry of a stream that never connected, the kept count across a replaced session, the stop on a non-transient error, the stable-stream threshold, or the reset after it.
- Independent review (subagent): the state machine, cleanup and unchanged Stop and Resume paths checked out; it found the unbounded connect-then-drop loop and the three untested bounds above, now fixed and covered.
  Its other notes are the known limits above (another viewer's Stop, Stop disabled while retrying, a close during another operation) and a cosmetic one: during attempts the status alternates between "Reconnecting to computer…" and "Connecting display…".
- PR #440 review (Opus, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra): fixed a replacement session's failed first ticket bypassing the retries, its ticket request missing the abort signal, the start budget not being rechecked after a wait, and the 10 s stable threshold letting a session revoked by every 15 s recheck loop forever; added tests for the retries, the budget and the threshold, for Reconnect after a 409 and for aborting an in-flight reconnect request (the replacement ticket's abort signal has no dedicated test).
  Round 2 found that the replacement-ticket handoff could override Stop: a pending Stop no longer races an automatic attempt (`reconnectAutomatically` returns while another operation is pending), and a ticket failure for a session that Stop already retired keeps "Computer stopped"; both orderings are tested.
  Declined: holding off renewal in a hidden tab (an open viewer keeping its worker alive is the documented behavior), and retrying the rare transient 409 on `POST /sessions`.
- Follow-ups after #440 (CodeRabbit and Opus review): starting also retries a homeserver that cannot be reached for the OpenID token (matrix-js-sdk `ConnectionError`), and new tests pin the effect's retired-session guard (a 403 after Stop keeps "Computer stopped") and manual Reconnect restoring the automatic attempts.
- Validation: `npx vitest run src/app/mindroom/computer/` (115 passed), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the 18 existing warnings), Prettier on both files, `npm run build`.
  `npm test`: 6,615 passed and 4 failed, the known `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` (1) cases.
  Not run: the live `e2e/worker-computer.spec.ts`, which needs the backend's computer fixture.
- Next: decide whether another viewer's Stop should stay stopped (needs a server answer that tells it apart); PR review; live check against a deployment that a worker restart and a session expiry reconnect without a click.

### Quiet thread summaries inside a thread (2026-10-09)

- Why: someone told the owner the automatic AI thread summaries were intrusive, large and obnoxious inside a thread. MindRoom posts one after the first reply and then every ten messages, each a glass card in 15px semibold, and since the summary describes the thread's lasting topic, most cards repeated the banner's title word for word. The owner had no strong view on the room timeline, so its card under a thread root is unchanged.
- Design: chosen from mockups (centered line, footnote, icon only). In an open thread a summary event is one muted line under the reply before it: "AI titled this thread" for the first, "AI title updated" for a change, "Title edited" for a manual summary. Hovering it with a mouse, or tapping or clicking it, shows the full summary, "AI summary of last N messages" and "Was: <old title>" struck through. Escape, a press elsewhere or moving keyboard focus on closes it; it follows the marker when the timeline scrolls. folds' `PopOut` layer covers the whole screen, so the details are a `role="tooltip"` layer with `pointer-events: none`: the marker, the timeline's wheel and the app's shortcuts (`hasBlockingPortalOverlay`) keep working while they show.
- A summary with the same text as the one before it in the thread leaves no row. `planThreadSummaryTimeline` (`threads/threadSummaryTimeline.ts`) walks the thread's events in order, skipping edits, reactions and ignored senders (rows the timeline hides) and comparing the text each row shows after its latest edit (the row's `getEditedEvent` and `getLatestMessageContent`, in the timeline set that holds the event), and returns the hidden ids plus, per shown summary, whether it is the first and the text it replaced. `useThreadSummaryTimeline` runs it for the open thread and runs it again when an encrypted thread event decrypts into a summary, because live events reach the thread before they decrypt. It listens by wire type (`isEncrypted()`), so a summary whose first attempt failed for want of a room key is still replanned when the key arrives. The earliest loaded summary only counts as the first once the SDK has loaded the thread and no older history is left on the server or in the cache (`threadInitialSdkLoaded`, `canPaginateThreadBack`, `threadHasMoreCachedBack`); until then it says "AI title updated". The route's event and a jump target stay visible even when they repeat, and keep showing after the route or the highlight moves on.
- The hidden ids join the approval timeline's into `hiddenThreadEventIds` in `MindroomRoomTimeline`, so they use the same zero-height, render-nothing path as hidden approval rows (row estimate, measurement, render, grouping context, renderable-reply count).
- `TimelineMessageBody` renders `MindroomThreadSummaryMarker` for a summary only when a thread is open; the room timeline and other surfaces keep `MindroomThreadSummaryCard`. Planner and row parse the summary the same way (`getMindroomThreadSummaryInfo`), so a legacy boolean-flag summary still renders as before and is never hidden.
- `estimateThreadEventRowHeight` estimates a summary at one line, the marker's height, instead of its full body.
- The banner's summary tints once (2.4 s, none with reduced motion) when it changes while the thread stays open; switching threads does not tint, and expanding the banner again does not replay it. The collapsed pill shows no title, so collapsing drops a pending tint.
- The marker uses folds' muted opacity (`config.opacity.P300`, 6.8:1 or more on the light surfaces; 0.6 was 4.2:1, below AA) and a logical inline margin for right-to-left catalogs.
- New keys in all 17 catalogs: `mindroomUi.messages.mindroomThreadSummaryMarker.{titled,updated,edited,previous}`; the popover reuses `sharedUi.threadSummary.*` for its provenance line.
- Known limits: the popover opens above the marker and can cover the reply above it. A cached title that a newer live one replaces right after a thread opens tints once. A routed-to repeat kept visible says "AI title updated". An event that decrypts between a render and the hook subscribing is replanned only at the next thread change.
- Tests: `threadSummaryTimeline.test.ts` (first, repeat, whitespace, replaced text, an edited summary, an edit between summaries, an ignored sender, each history flag, revealed route), `useThreadSummaryTimeline.test.tsx` (an encrypted repeat is hidden once it decrypts, and after a failed first attempt; each fails without its fix), `MindroomThreadSummaryMarker.test.tsx` (labels, hover, touch, tap, Escape, outside press, blur, scroll, pass-through layer, description), the one-line estimate in `threadRenderUtils.test.ts`, `TimelineMessageFeature.test.tsx` (marker in a thread, card outside), `RoomTimeline.threadSummaryMarkers.test.ts` (a repeat leaves no row, failing with the hiding removed; a routed-to repeat stays after the route moves on, failing without the sticky reveal; a summary is compared by its latest edit, failing without the timeline's `getContent`), and the banner tint in `ThreadContextBanner.test.ts` (once per change, not after collapsing). The shared timeline harness's virtualizer gained `resizeItem`.
- Live: new `thread-summary-marker.spec.ts` (desktop hover, moves within the marker, click to pin; phone tap) against a disposable Tuwunel. While the details show, it checks the point under the marker is still the marker and no portal child blocks input; that check failed with the pass-through removed. Also passing: `thread-banner-height-anchor`, `thread-banner-overlay`, `thread-banner-collapse` (desktop, tablet, phone), `cinny060`/`cinny061` summary specs, `thread-summary-background-cache`, `thread-cache-loading` and the Arabic/Japanese summary case of `i18n-complete-live` pass. One run of the height-anchor spec's "summary arriving" case failed while logging in, then passed three times in a row.
- Validation: typecheck, build and ESLint (0 errors) pass. `npm test`: everything passes except `xcodeCloudPostClone.test.ts` (3) and one `useRoomInputSendSessionController.test.ts` case, which fail the same way on an unchanged `dev` checkout here.

### Undo typing one word at a time in the composer (2026-10-09)

- Why: the owner found Cmd/Ctrl+Z in the composer too aggressive; after typing a sentence, one undo removed the whole sentence.
- Cause: slate-history's `shouldMerge` folds every `insert_text` that continues the previous one into the same undo batch, with no word or pause boundary, so an unbroken run of typing was a single undo step.
- `withWordUndo` (`components/editor/history.ts`), applied directly around `withHistory` in `useEditor`, starts a new batch when a keystroke begins a word after whitespace. Undo after "hello world again" leaves "hello world ", then "hello ", then nothing; redo steps forward the same way. It only acts on the first saved op of a change (selection ops before it are fine; slate-react's Android input manager and `beforeinput` often select first) and only when no caller set a merge mode, so a paste or a transform that inserts several words stays one step. Deleting is unchanged. Every composer and the message editor share `useEditor`.
- Known limits: slate-history keeps the last 100 undo steps, which is now about 100 words of typing instead of 100 runs. Text written without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) still undoes a whole typed run at once.
- Tests: `history.test.ts` covers word steps, a single word, runs of spaces, a pasted sentence after typed text, a multi-word transform, a keystroke that selects first, a caller's `withMerging`, and redo. The new fixture `e2e/fixtures/composer-undo.html` mounts the real `CustomEditor`; `composer-undo.spec.ts` types with the keyboard and presses Ctrl/Cmd+Z. It fails without `withWordUndo` (the first undo empties the composer) and passes in Chromium, and in Firefox and WebKit in the `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.2-noble` container. The spec leaves redo to the unit test: Playwright's Desktop Safari sends a Mac user agent, so slate-react wants Cmd+Shift+Z there while a Linux host presses Ctrl.

Sticker and Emoji reuse the emoji board's tab names (`sharedUi.tabs.*`).

### Open a conversation's canvases and computer from the room header (2026-10-08)

- Why: a canvas an agent keeps updating was easy to lose, because after closing it the only way back was its **Open panel** button far up the conversation, or the global Canvases page.
  The header's Computer button also showed in every room with an agent, though most never use their computer.
- Status: implemented on `feat/conversation-panel-buttons` (commits on top of `911d50c1`), validated below.
  Live canvas specs pass against a disposable Tuwunel.
  Not yet merged or deployed.
  The worker-computer spec's edit (see below) has not been run live here, because it needs the backend's computer fixture.
  The backend half (the first browser call in a thread sends the `show_computer` notice) is a separate mindroom PR; the two merge in either order.
- Header Canvas button (`CanvasHeaderButton`, icon `Icons.Category`, the sidebar's Canvases icon) sits after the Computer button.
  It shows only where canvases are on, outside a call, and when the conversation (the routed thread, or the room's main timeline) has a listed canvas.
  With one canvas it toggles it (`Show Canvas` / `Hide Canvas`, `aria-pressed`); with several it opens a menu titled `Canvases`, newest update first, each row with its title and update time, the open one marked (`aria-current="true"` and a check).
  Choosing the open one closes it, another opens it, and a reordering update keeps the menu open.
  Opening goes through `useOpenCanvasById` (`loadCanvasEvent`, then the Chat UI action `activate`), the same validated path as the timeline button, so call and disabled-canvas rules, panel exclusivity and the latest version apply; a canvas whose request was deleted opens nothing.
  New keys `mindroomUi.threads.mindroomRoomViewHeader.showCanvas`, `hideCanvas` and `canvases` in all 17 catalogs.
- Computer button: the header button shows only when the computer is available and either its panel is open or this conversation received a valid `show_computer` notice (sent when an agent calls `chat_ui.show_computer()`).
  Otherwise the room's More menu offers **Show computer** (also in Simple Mode), so users can still open it first, for example to log in; once open, the header button appears and the menu item goes.
  On phones the header never shows the Computer button, so the More menu always opens it there (at most Schedules, Canvas, Pinned, Call, Members and More: six actions, as before this change).
  Timeline **View computer** buttons and automatic opening are unchanged.
- Index: the canvas index database (`mindroom-canvas-index::<session>`) is now version 2.
  The upgrade adds the object store `computerShown` (rows `{ key, roomId, threadId }`, key `roomId`, newline, `threadId`) and keeps the `canvases` rows.
  Rolling back to a build older than this one makes the old build's canvas index fail to open (`VersionError`), so its Canvases list stays empty until the next login deletes the database.
  A listed canvas whose agent left the room opens nothing from the header, as on the Canvases page (accepted).
  The recorder parses `show_computer` notices with `readChatUiAction` (sender, requester, membership, echo and edit checks), so a notice for another user, from a non-agent or from a local echo records nothing.
  `useConversationCanvases`, `useComputerShown` and `useHasListedCanvases` read the index through `watchCanvasIndex`, the one subscribe, read and debounce helper the Canvases page shares; the two conversation hooks share one keyed helper, so the key rules live in one place.
  The index is still deleted at logout, and a canvas or computer notice this browser never received is not known.
  The recorder runs where canvases or a computer service are on (`CanvasIndexFeature`, tested in `MindroomClientNonUIFeatures.test.ts`), because the two are separate opt-ins and the header's Computer button needs the notice where only the computer is.
- Label: the timeline button `mindroomUi.uiActions.openCanvas` reads **Open canvas** (was **Open panel**).
  The 16 other catalogs already named a canvas with their word for "panel" (`mindroomUi.canvases.canvas`), so their `openCanvas` text already matches and did not change; the English catalog and the component's default value did.
  `e2e/agent-canvas.spec.ts` matches the new name.
- Tests: `canvasIndexStore.test.ts` (computer notices per conversation, upgrade from version 1 keeps canvases, listeners notified), `canvasIndex.test.tsx` (what the recorder keeps and ignores, per-conversation filtering and order, no commit for writes that leave an answer as it was, `useOpenCanvasById`), `CanvasHeaderButton.test.tsx` (hidden, toggle, menu order and open mark, choices, reordering with the menu open, menu dropped at one canvas), `RoomViewHeader.test.ts` (the computer button and menu item for every availability, shown and open combination, and on phones only the menu item; the item opens the computer and closes the menu; kept in Simple Mode; the Canvas button with its canvases and handlers, absent without them), `RoomView.test.ts` and `Room.test.ts` (the room passes the canvas and computer state through, nothing during a call or with canvases off).
- Live: `e2e/agent-canvas.spec.ts` gains "the room header brings back a conversation's canvases".
  In one thread the agent sends a canvas and then a second: the button first toggles the single canvas directly, then lists both newest first, a choice shows its canvas, and the open one is marked.
  A second thread in the room starts with no button and toggles its own single canvas without a menu, and the first thread still lists only its two.
  The sidebar's Canvases tab shares the menu button's name, so the spec looks in the room header only.
  `e2e/worker-computer.spec.ts` now opens the computer through More Options, Show Computer, because its thread has no `show_computer` notice and the header button stays hidden until the computer is open.
- Validation (Node 24.21): `npm test` 6,528 passed and 3 failed (`xcodeCloudPostClone`, no `/bin/bash` on this NixOS host; they pass in CI), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, 18 existing warnings), `npm run build`, branch-wide Prettier.
  Live, against a disposable Tuwunel on port 28258 with the production build in Playwright 1.58.2's Ubuntu image: `agent-canvas.spec.ts` (2 cases), `agent-canvas-list.spec.ts` and `agent-ui-actions.spec.ts` pass directly, and the scheduler passes the two canvas specs (`node scripts/test-e2e-parallel.mjs --jobs 2 e2e/agent-canvas.spec.ts e2e/agent-canvas-list.spec.ts`).
  `npm run test:e2e:parallel -- --list` discovers the new case.
- Next, not done: run `e2e/worker-computer.spec.ts` where the backend's computer fixture exists; merge with the backend PR; deployed check that a thread with a canvas and a browsing agent shows both header buttons.
  Deferred review notes: the hooks answer empty until the first read after a conversation switch, so a header button can appear a moment late; the hooks read IndexedDB even where canvases are off.
- PR review round 1 (2026-10-08, mindroom-chat#436):
  A header open whose canvas had to be fetched could land in the wrong conversation: after a switch to another thread of the same room, the first thread's captured `activate` accepted the canvas but performed the second thread's action.
  `openCanvasById` is replaced by `useOpenCanvasById`, which drops the answer when the conversation (room and routed and root thread) changed or the room left meanwhile, drops it when a later choice superseded it, and acts through the latest `activate`.
  `Room.test.ts` and `canvasIndex.test.tsx` fail without the guard (a deferred `/relations` answer after a thread switch, an unmount, and a later choice).
  The canvas menu is bounded to the viewport (`maxHeight: calc(100vh - 6rem)`, flex column) with the choices in a Folds `Scroll`, so with many canvases on a short window the lower choices stay reachable.
  `CanvasHeaderButton.test.tsx` pins the scroll area inside the bounded menu, and `e2e/agent-canvas.spec.ts` sends ten more canvases, shrinks the window to 480 px high, checks the menu ends on screen and scrolls to the oldest choice, which opens.
  The trigger no longer sets `aria-haspopup="menu"` or `aria-expanded`: the glass menus render no `menu` or `menuitem` roles, and the room's More and pinned-messages triggers use `aria-pressed` only.
  `useConversationCanvases` and `useComputerShown` keep the held answer when a read equals it (same `canvasId`, `revisionId`, `updatedTs` and `title` per canvas, or the same boolean), so an index write elsewhere no longer renders the room; `useHasListedCanvases` moved onto `watchCanvasIndex` and keeps its `listedBySession` cache.
  Validation: focused vitest, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, branch-wide Prettier, and `e2e/agent-canvas.spec.ts` plus `e2e/agent-canvas-list.spec.ts` live against a disposable Tuwunel (3 passed).
- PR review round 2 (2026-10-08, mindroom-chat#436):
  A header open still loading was undone by nothing but another header open, so closing the canvas, opening Members or opening the computer meanwhile was overridden when the fetch answered.
  `useOpenCanvasById` now takes a context string and drops the answer from the commit of any change in it; `Room` builds it from the conversation and the side-panel state (open canvas ID, computer open, Members open), so any later user panel action wins.
  `Room.test.ts` covers a close from the panel and from the header, Members and the computer opened while the fetch is pending, and the thread-switch test also checks the late answer does not navigate back; each fails without the panel state in the context.
  On phones the Computer entry is always the More menu item, which keeps the header at its former worst case of six actions (with canvases, a recorded notice and a callable agent it held seven, clipping More Options at 320 px); `RoomViewHeader.test.ts` covers phones, and desktop and tablet keep the button.
  `RoomViewHeader.test.ts` also fails now when the Canvas button is dropped from the header.
  The menu style is private to its module, a test title no longer claims an order, and the attribute-absence test is gone.
  The Runbook records that a rollback below this build leaves the Canvases list empty until the next login, and that a listed canvas whose agent left opens nothing from the header (accepted).
  Validation: focused vitest, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, branch-wide Prettier.

### Collapse the thread banner to a pill; resolver after the title (2026-10-08)

- Why: the owner found the expanded banner out of balance with a resolved thread, and wanted the collapsed banner much smaller, with the toggle moved into More.
  The "by …" byline sat under the Resolved chip, so that column was about twice as tall as the buttons beside it; they centered against it, leaving the chip above them and the byline below.
- Collapsing moved from a chevron at the end of the bar to More (`Hide thread details`, `data-thread-action="hideDetails"`, last item). `ThreadActionsMenu` shows it only when given `onHideDetails`; the banner passes it while expanded, the thread list never does.
- Collapsed, the banner is a pill at the start of the row with back and `Show thread details` only (`width: fit-content`, padding `S100`), so the messages show beside it instead of under a full-width bar. It keeps the resolved tint, and an active permissions grant stays in it. Since the pill always hides something (at least the title), the `canCollapse` rules and the `Collapsed` selectors in the compact styles are gone; `CompactHidden` and `whenCompact` now only serve short landscape screens, which keep their one-row layout unless the setting is on. `ShortViewportHidden` and `ResolveChip` are deleted. The setting is still `threadBannerCollapsed`.
- The toggling button unmounts with the layout it toggles, so focus moves to the control that toggles back: `Show thread details` after hiding, More after showing (the banner itself while More is disabled for an unconfirmed thread root).
- Fixed on the way: closing the banner's More menu restored focus to More with a plain `focus()`, which scrolled the thread to its first message (the sticky banner's place in the flow; `scrollTop` 0). Both focus moves now pass `preventScroll`. The live spec caught it once the menu became the way to collapse.
- The resolver byline (`✓ by …`, `role="img"` labelled `Resolved by …`) follows the title in the subtitle row like the schedule, after a `·` separator when there is a title. Where the title column is 26rem or narrower it takes its own line under the title, without the separator: beside the title it squeezed the title to "E…" on a phone, and nearly as far on a tablet with the room list open. The title column is a size container (`containerType: 'inline-size'`) for this, since the viewport width does not tell how much room the title has. A pinned thread still shows neither.
- Resolve is an icon button like More and the pin (`Icons.Check`, same size and radius), after the owner found the text chip still out of place beside them. Resolved, it is solid green (`ResolvedButton`, the `Success` main colours the chip had), the way a set pin is filled. Its accessible names stay "Resolve" and "Resolved", and the Resolved button is described by the byline (`aria-describedby`), so screen readers still hear "Resolved by …" where the native `title` used to say it, also on short screens, which hide the byline.
- More, the pin, Resolve and the pill's Show details name themselves in folds tooltips below them (`BannerTooltip`) instead of native `title`s. Resolved, the tooltip reads "Resolved by …" with "Reopen thread" under it for those who can reopen. More and Show details merge the tooltip's trigger ref with the refs the focus moves use; folds' trigger ref only stores the node, so the inline ref callbacks are safe.
- The title (`SummaryText`) is capped at `max-content`, so a byline or a schedule follows it instead of sitting at the far end of the row on wide screens; it still shrinks and truncates first.
- Tests: `ThreadContextBanner.test.ts`: short-screen hiding (now including the byline), collapsing from More and carrying the setting to the next thread with focus on Show details and then More, focus on the banner when More is disabled, the tint and no Hide item once collapsed, the byline in the subtitle row with and without a title and absent when pinned, Resolve as a check icon button with the tooltips (who resolved it, plus "Reopen thread" only for editors) and no native `title` on the buttons, `preventScroll` on both focus moves (fails with plain `focus()`). `ThreadActionsMenu.test.tsx`: the item only with `onHideDetails`, last, closing after hiding.
- Live: `thread-banner-collapse.spec.ts` (desktop 1280×800, tablet 820×1180 with the room list open, phone 390×844) now collapses from More: two buttons left, at most 80 × 44 px, reader still at the latest reply, kept after a reload; Show details restores tags and Resolve and focuses More; resolving shows the byline beside the title on desktop (within 16 px of its end) and below it on the tablet and the phone (title wider than 100 px), with the check button centered on More, the same size, a different (green) background and the accessible description "Resolved by …"; on desktop, pointing at it shows the tooltip with "Resolved by" and "Reopen thread". The tablet case was added after review found the byline squeezing the title there while it wrapped by viewport width. The spec failed at "reader at the latest reply" before the `preventScroll` fix (gap 320 px). `compact-card-display-names.spec.ts` now expects the byline's text to contain `by <name>` (a separator can precede it), checks its label, and reads "Resolved by <name>" from the Resolved button's tooltip instead of its `title`. Also passing: all four `short-viewport-chrome.spec.ts` cases and the three `thread-banner-height-anchor.spec.ts` cases, each run alone.
